description:3502d1273c262a3cafe148b9.text: A witch’s words will seal your fate.

description:f5b18c844b79897858b97f1f.text: Watch for a crimson sun’s warning.

description:576a95f98d0d6d7e985673d4.text: Too much dreaming will hold your mind captive.

description:d6c05ad0f96815ea07d4ea9e.text: Do not disturb roots beneath slumbering trees.

description:1ea82d6dc058d08e556d9b94.text: Beneath Morrslieb, hold your breath against the darkness seeking your soul.

description:e72c2e42436b7d352e33c418.text: Dread a country where no gull cries.

description:e95c9f42d0ddbdd36f3181cb.text: Show impiety on Mondstille and no further night will come for you.

description:ab73624fb0e31aa0db7666f9.text: On Festag, no bridge is safe to trust.

description:2d1ac8818c0f64a06418ddb4.text: When Ulric’s children summon you, haste will bring your fall.

description:76bc322d4035ee0ac0bd346e.text: A silent night foretells a dawn you will never see.

description:7f54409004d4991946cf5c7b.text: A missing key will be your undoing.

description:82e3c0659702629210b1c76f.text: Even an ogre who treasures you remains an ogre.

description:9af39979c327dc136d7ace05.text: One toll brings peace, two bring pleasure, and three bring death.

description:a3376824283ff35c87059573.text: Your end approaches on strings held by the Twisted Puppeteer.

description:eae0d99119fc599a81422d4a.text: Do not follow Ottokar’s example by courting a god.

description:7df21b783b2a9be00d121275.text: Remember Tomas: leave the woodland beast unprovoked.

description:f7486be12b94a30b732b7f11.text: Sickness and plague will soon bring you low.

description:1cd4c8f6c4d5427fa3a5381a.text: A sword will bring you death rather than justice.

description:82ce4ab8e28245baf085c0f8.text: Beware sticky buns, pork pasties, and eel-and-leek pies: Morr serves them all.

description:a988f56bf8040c6a29325efa.text: Do not exhaust a tired Shallyan’s patience.

description:970a6d41ef20c0a70fd9e143.text: Treasure hunters will meet an ambusher wearing a goblin’s shape.

description:11097534646fbf38bbf569d7.text: Settle your debts, remembering Baron Trister.

description:9ccedeecf93de5564973a13f.text: Carry a crow-skull relic against a fatal draught of poison.

description:5b71647ecd672d5240f00fc4.text: Win or lose your wagers with Elves honestly.

description:1e3506f3b2d47a4bf7342851.text: Mock another’s wind and your own bowels will rot.

description:2487d65f634c3397867f14a0.text: Your drowning will come on dry ground.

description:a13d7a3d868a4f3115500d28.text: The cry of a newborn will herald Morr’s welcome.

description:b59de9fe6987764ef97d9a69.text: A siren’s song must be heeded, lest your heart stop.

description:dfd48375d9f1328875ce0407.text: Wake before Cacklefax calls and death will find you early.

description:92a7e624b22ffb6ceab86911.text: A maiden will come from Morr.

description:d3a6b6597e6a409e4a402c30.name: Badger Rider
description:d3a6b6597e6a409e4a402c30.text: Mootland Halflings only (p. 87). Requires GM approval: at creation, persuade the GM that Badger Riders exist and perform their terrifying war cry for the group (p. 87).

description:1a1ea0ad8b8a4a5c114a46d6.name: Thorncobble clan (Reikland)
description:1a1ea0ad8b8a4a5c114a46d6.text: A Thorncobble may start as a Noble if they have Noble Blood (p. 31). Select Noble in Careers; export requires that Talent.

description:509ecf00f09caf82e6e3e3f3.name: Mootland
description:509ecf00f09caf82e6e3e3f3.text: Mootland Halflings can select Fieldwarden or, with GM approval and the required war cry, Badger Rider. A random Road Warden or Soldier result can instead become the corresponding Career (p. 87).

description:553776a275f9f5d244d2f9b8.name: Eonir — Cityborn (Toriour)
description:553776a275f9f5d244d2f9b8.text: GM option: retain Wood Elf starting attributes but select from High Elf Careers. Record Wood Elf (Eonir) as Species and Cityborn on the Class line (p. 78).

description:46c4a950b2bc89f6500c92bf.name: Eonir — Younger (Harioth)
description:46c4a950b2bc89f6500c92bf.text: Use Wood Elf Careers and add Youngblood. Among Eonir, count as lower Status unless the other character also has Youngblood (p. 78). This comparison does not reduce Career Status.

description:4c508d25d9623b348e7d300e.name: Options: Halfling Clan Skills and Talents
description:4c508d25d9623b348e7d300e.text:
At creation, Halflings may add the listed clan options to these Species lists.

|  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Clan | Additional Skills | Additional Talent |
| Ashfield | Cool, Intuition, Language (Mootish), Ranged (any) | Acute Sense (Sight) or Etiquette (Soldiers) |
| Brambledown | Language (Mootish), Navigation, Outdoor Survival, Swim | Gregarious or Seasoned Traveller |
| Brandysnap | Animal Care, Gamble, Language (Mootish), Lore (Herbs) | Craftsman (Farmer) or Sturdy |
| Hayfoot | Gamble, Haggle, Evaluate, Language (Mootish) | Dealmaker or Etiquette (Guilders) |
| Hollyfoot | Evaluate, Haggle, Language (Mootish), Trade (Any) | Craftsman (Any) or Nimble-Fingered |
| Hayfoot-Hollyfoot | Bribery, Haggle, Gossip, Language (Mootish) | Argumentative or Numismatics |
| Lostpockets | Endurance, Gamble, Gossip, Intuition | Hardy or Stone Soup |
| Lowhaven | Bribery, Haggle, Intimidate, Language (Mootish) | Criminal or Etiquette (Criminals or Guilders) |
| Rumster | Endurance, Gossip, Haggle, Language (Mootish) | Craftsman (Cook) or Dealmaker |
| Skelfsider | Endurance, Gamble, Gossip, Language (Mootish) | Beneath Notice or Etiquette (Servants) |
| Thorncobble | Gossip, Leadership, Lore (Heraldry), Language (Mootish) | Etiquette (Nobles or Scholars) or Read/Write |
| Tumbleberry | Gossip, Haggle, Lore (Any), Language (Mootish) | Etiquette (Burghers or Guilders) or Read/Write |

Species Skills: Charm, Consume Alcohol, Lore (Reikland), Perception, Sleight of Hand, Stealth (Any), Trade (Cook), 4 Clan Skills.

Species Talents: Acute Sense (Taste), Night Vision, Resistance (Chaos), Small, 1 Clan Talent, 1 Random Talent.

description:3c64713c7918bafb365593dd.name: Wymund the Anchorite
description:3c64713c7918bafb365593dd.text: Patient scrutiny and loyalty mark this sign; forgiveness can become costly, and a final rejection implacable.

description:2437a7cab1ab553f3e78c4d4.name: The Big Cross
description:2437a7cab1ab553f3e78c4d4.text: This sign favours certainty and sensible choices, with a risk of passivity unless given a cause to pursue.

description:b5bd6996f37f1b614b8a8e61.name: The Limner’s Line
description:b5bd6996f37f1b614b8a8e61.text: A creative sign associated with artistry in any profession and a tendency towards excessive self-criticism.

description:10190b2ba4f68bc635a9156c.name: Gnuthus the Ox
description:10190b2ba4f68bc635a9156c.text: Loyalty, honesty and keeping promises define this sign; misplaced trust or allegiance may prove costly.

description:e5bb28454c859aba9018ac2f.name: Dragomas the Drake
description:e5bb28454c859aba9018ac2f.text: Confidence and natural leadership characterise this sign, with a risk of arrogance and tyranny.

description:39660c19f0ef504aaf035f3e.name: The Gloaming
description:39660c19f0ef504aaf035f3e.text: Scepticism can produce able investigators and scholars, but also suspicion and distrust of anything beyond physical proof, even among those drawn to magic.

description:e1684df6f61e30aea053e26b.name: Grungni’s Baldric
description:e1684df6f61e30aea053e26b.text: This sign favours honour, discipline and a soldier’s rigour; relaxation and humour may come less easily.

description:6e308604a7b43cb11422f709.name: Mammit the Wise
description:6e308604a7b43cb11422f709.text: Curiosity and reflection encourage fairness and learning, but detached study of others’ suffering can become cruelty.

description:66a67ac778ee7c2db9ee45e8.name: Mummit the Fool
description:66a67ac778ee7c2db9ee45e8.text: Intuition, good sense and apparent luck accompany a tendency towards impulsiveness, wandering and avoiding responsibility.

description:d08e52a0bfc306c236df66c5.name: The Two Bullocks
description:d08e52a0bfc306c236df66c5.text: Diligent inventors seek useful improvements for others, though impractical projects and manipulated idealism can lead them astray.

description:3a5d9adb897e3f631a7bf10f.name: The Dancer
description:3a5d9adb897e3f631a7bf10f.text: Passionate commitment can become obsession, and rejection may provoke violence. Impassioned Zeal’s focus can be selected later in play (p. 43).

description:cc56c7b07f054ba409bcfa5f.name: The Drummer
description:cc56c7b07f054ba409bcfa5f.text: Generosity and enthusiasm for company mark this sign, but unchecked indulgence can become ruinous.

description:c0418fef298ba3f83ec3225e.name: The Piper
description:c0418fef298ba3f83ec3225e.text: Tact and cunning favour diplomacy and theft; self-interest may override loyalty. The associated deity is disputed, and Marienburg considers the sign fortunate.

description:2860f04d16d6ae403703c527.name: Vobist the Faint
description:2860f04d16d6ae403703c527.text: An apparently uncertain temperament can alternate between caution and surprising courage, reflecting an instinct for choosing battles. A full Morrslieb during its ascendance is an ill omen.

description:0e63651501ee97953f6bc73b.name: The Broken Cart
description:0e63651501ee97953f6bc73b.text: Concern for status and possessions can become confidence once insecurity fades. The sign’s widely recognised link to disease conceals a rarely admitted association with Nurgle; desperation can draw people towards forbidden offerings.

description:e4ee1568a18798554293ad59.name: The Greased Goat
description:e4ee1568a18798554293ad59.text: Fear of disappointment can create distance and self-pity, though rare happiness spreads to others. Magically gifted children of this sign often favour Ghur.

description:085f3f0cf2e34634570b5901.name: Rhya’s Cauldron
description:085f3f0cf2e34634570b5901.text: Associated with life’s growth and death, this sign favours mercy and justice; relentless pursuit of ideals can disregard others’ welfare. Astromancers, astrologers, and Jade and Amethyst Wizards revere it.

description:b2fc4512db99cb24df953f23.name: Cackelfax the Cockerel
description:b2fc4512db99cb24df953f23.text: Ambition and practical acquisition of wealth, skills, influence and connections define this sign. Loyalty to supporters may accompany greed or ruthlessness.

description:cef1c042ce554d627544d23e.name: The Bonesaw
description:cef1c042ce554d627544d23e.text: An enquiring sign that seeks experiments, exploration and widespread sharing of knowledge, sometimes appearing overbearing.

description:5e9903e7ef1a031b856f6b39.name: The Witchling Star
description:5e9903e7ef1a031b856f6b39.text: This ominous magical sign suggests courage, adaptability and charm, together with a changeable nature that can trouble companions.

description:6849453d545666ecd1099352.name: Ogre Club
description:6849453d545666ecd1099352.text: Optional modifications (p. 30): metal plates grant Pummel, rusty spikes grant Penetrating, and scavenged blades grant Hack. Quality/Flaw editing is deferred; the creator selects none automatically. Price and Encumbrance already reflect Ogre size; do not double them. Availability applies in the Empire (p. 29). Average creatures can barely use these weapons; ask the GM (p. 28).

description:a3f6fbf72853f20cedbf4a43.name: Ironfist
description:a3f6fbf72853f20cedbf4a43.text: An Ironfist cannot be disarmed from an Ogre. Its hand remains usable for holding a weapon and simple actions (p. 30). Price and Encumbrance already reflect Ogre size; do not double them. Availability applies in the Empire (p. 29). Average creatures can barely use these weapons; ask the GM (p. 28).

description:126a41a59e174a99bea398af.name: Big Ogre Club (2H)
description:126a41a59e174a99bea398af.text: Optional modifications (p. 30): metal plates grant Pummel, rusty spikes grant Penetrating, and scavenged blades grant Hack. Quality/Flaw editing is deferred; the creator selects none automatically. Price and Encumbrance already reflect Ogre size; do not double them. Availability applies in the Empire (p. 29). Average creatures can barely use these weapons; ask the GM (p. 28).

description:1ee9e58eadfc302f39280741.name: Great Throwing Spear
description:1ee9e58eadfc302f39280741.text: Ogre Hunter javelin (p. 30). Price and Encumbrance already reflect Ogre size; do not double them. Availability applies in the Empire (p. 29). Average creatures can barely use these weapons; ask the GM (p. 28).

description:c8631359c41418b0c5ec5128.name: Leadbelcher Gun (2H)
description:c8631359c41418b0c5ec5128.text: Fires shot or cannonballs (p. 30). Inherent Blackpowder and Damaging Qualities follow core p. 303. Price and Encumbrance already reflect Ogre size; do not double them. Availability applies in the Empire (p. 29). Average creatures can barely use these weapons; ask the GM (p. 28).

description:a9518cc824894a4e6c260da5.name: Ogre Pistol
description:a9518cc824894a4e6c260da5.text: Uses standard blackpowder shot and powder. It also functions as a Hand Weapon and breaks only on a Fumbled attack (p. 30); this grants no separate weapon. Inherent Blackpowder and Damaging Qualities follow core p. 303. Price and Encumbrance already reflect Ogre size; do not double them. Availability applies in the Empire (p. 29). Average creatures can barely use these weapons; ask the GM (p. 28).

description:29aa13c5292498cadc8ce9ce.name: Harpoon Launcher
description:29aa13c5292498cadc8ce9ce.text: Use Ranged (Crossbow) or Ranged (Entangling), without penalty. The profile includes the rope; removing it gives range 60 and removes Entangle (p. 30). Price and Encumbrance already reflect Ogre size; do not double them. Availability applies in the Empire (p. 29). Average creatures can barely use these weapons; ask the GM (p. 28).

description:857a3ee20ef81aa7e00bb26d.name: Chain Trap
description:857a3ee20ef81aa7e00bb26d.text: Throw the chained jaws at prey, then reel the target in (p. 30). Price and Encumbrance already reflect Ogre size; do not double them. Availability applies in the Empire (p. 29). Average creatures can barely use these weapons; ask the GM (p. 28).

description:03a838153ac55b2818ddc4d8.name: Vice
description:03a838153ac55b2818ddc4d8.text: When faced with your Vice, make a Psychology Test (Fourth Edition p. 190). description:420efcc741a4ac754e0faa92.name: Identifying A Magical Artefact
description:420efcc741a4ac754e0faa92.text:
Detect Artefact allows Intuition on touching the item (WFRP page 135). Other Wizards normally spend one week per attempt in a suitable laboratory, equipped library or ritual space, then make Challenging (+0) Lore (Magic).

|  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SL | Result | Consequences |
| +6 or more | Astounding Success | Identify the item and every Quirk. |
| +4 to +5 | Impressive Success | Identify the item and whether it has Quirks; the GM may conceal one Quirk’s details. |
| +2 to +3 | Success | Identify the item and visible Quirks, but no hidden ones. |
| +0 to +1 | Marginal Success | Identify the item and one hidden quirk. |
| 0 to -1 | Marginal Failure | Identification fails and is known to have failed. Clearly visible Quirks are recognised. |
| -2 to -3 | Failure | Misidentify it as a similar item; recognise clearly visible Quirks. |
| -4 to -5 | Impressive Failure | Misidentify it as a similar item; recognise clearly visible Quirks and wrongly infer one further Quirk. |
| -6 or less | Astounding Failure | Misidentify it as a similar item; recognise clearly visible Quirks and wrongly infer at least two further Quirks. |

description:6389d13c0f92c9c6a0bce99f.name: The Finished Result
description:6389d13c0f92c9c6a0bce99f.text:
Make final Challenging (+0) Lore (Magic) and Trade Tests; add their SL for this table.

|  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SL | Result | Consequences |
| +6 or more | Astounding Success | The item gains Unbreakable. |
| +4 to +5 | Impressive Success | Create without complications; add one chosen Item Quality (WFRP page 292). |
| +2 to +3 | Success | Create without complications. |
| 0 to +1 | Marginal Success | Create without flaws, taking 50% longer. |
| 0 to -11 | Marginal Failure | Create with one Quirk or curse from page 56. Reroll no-effect or Dwarf-rune results with +40. |
| -2 to -3 | Failure | Roll two Quirks or Curses with +40; reroll no-effect and Dwarf-rune results. Also choose one Item Flaw (WFRP page 292). |
| -4 to -5 | Impressive Failure | The artefact is useless; restart creation. |
| -6 or less-6 or less | Astounding Failure | The artefact explodes, causing a Bomb-equivalent hit (WFRP page 295). |

description:3e06365beef48ff811432b88.name: Quirks And Curses
description:3e06365beef48ff811432b88.text:
For a random artefact, the GM secretly rolls for Quirks or Curses. Scrolls are exempt; most staffs are traditionally uncursed.

| D100 | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| 01–20 | No Quirk or Curse. |
| 21–35 | Each use emits blue-green light. Choose an Imperial god whose rites helped make it; Shallya does not assist weapon-making. The magic requires 32 consecutive days following that god’s strictures (WFRP Chapter 7). |
| 36–40 | Dwarf runes grant Durable and Fine, with no negative item effect. Its makers may seek its return and consider the bearer a thief. Its constant humming makes Stealth Tests one step harder. |
| 41–45 | Activation requires a GM-chosen word that may need to be discovered. |
| 46–50 | Each use requires Very Easy (+60) Channelling; failure triggers Minor Miscast (WFRP page 234). No Skill means automatic failure. |
| 51–63 | Its magical abilities end after 1d100 days. |
| 64–69 | The bearer must eat twice their usual food or have a permanent Fatigued Condition while carrying it. |
| 70–75 | Ugly; its disturbing appearance may frighten superstitious people and attract Witch Hunters. |
| 76–78 | Minor Corruption source (WFRP page 182). |
| 79–80 | Works outdoors only, by day or night according to 1d10: 1–6 The Sun, 7–9 Mannslieb, 10 Morrslieb. Never works indoors or underground. |
| 81–84 | Tests using it suffer -1SL with others present and gain +1SL when alone. |
| 85–89 | Each use requires Challenging (+0) Endurance; failure causes Fatigued. |
| 90–93 | Unreliable. |
| D100 | Effect |
| --- | --- |

For the next 24 hours it may cast three Lore of Life spells with WP 47 to obstruct or humiliate the bearer, including healing enemies. A freed Spite may torment its rescuers. |

| 61–63 | Of the Wolf ’s Wide Jaws: Damaging. |
| 64–66 | Of Deft and Cunning: +20 WS or BS as appropriate. |
| 67–69 | Of Salt and Brine: The bearer gains a free Action in every combat’s first Round; also Fast. |
| 70–72 | Of Grisly Wounds: Damaging. |
| 73–75 | Of Tooth and Claw: Bestial creatures must pass Difficult (–10) Willpower before attacking the wielder. |
| 76–78 | Of Deepest Banishing: Count three additional Advantage when resolving Unstable. |
| 79–81 | Of Undue Substance: Pummel and Hack. |
| 82–84 | Of Languishing Death: Inflicted Wounds are Festering Wounds (WFRP page 187). |
| 85–87 | Of Keenest Edge: Hack, Impale and Penetrating, including ammunition fired. |
| 88–90 | Of Bane: Double Wounds inflicted on a Creature type from page 55’s Random Creature Table. |
| 91–92 | Of Ceaseless Cleaving: A damaging hit adds two Wounds. |
| 93–94 | Of Leaping Gold: Fast, Penetrating and Precise. |
| 95–96 | Of Grievous Injury: On Critical Injuries rolls (WFRP page 174), optionally reverse digits and use the more damaging result. |
| 97–98 | Of Form Mercurial: Each round choose from Fast, Hack, Impale, Penetrating and Precise. |
| 99 | Hoarfrost Blade: A damaging hit doubles Wounds, then adds four. Ranged weapons cannot confer this to ammunition; a ranged result gives 1d10 affected ammunition pieces instead. Ignore if the ranged weapon already has Legendary Weapon. |
| 00 | Legendary Weapon: Roll twice more; maximum five abilities. Duplicates do not stack. |

A wielder actively uses it as their primary combat weapon; a bearer holds it or carries it in a scabbard. All magical weapons harm creatures immune to non-magical attacks, including Ethereal creatures. Extra Qualities never stack; Fast twice does not impose –20 to defend.

description:422b6e2e95a9ffc5a380741a.name: Magical Weapon History Table
description:422b6e2e95a9ffc5a380741a.text:
| D100 | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| 01–17 | No special historical significance. |
| 18–29 | Battered: Choose Ugly, Shoddy or Unreliable. |
| 30–37 | Expertly Forged: Choose Fine, Durable, Lightweight or Practical. |
| 38–44 | Tyrant Borne: Champions of common people recognising its oppressive history may have Prejudice toward the bearer (WFRP page 190). |
| 45–51 | Sacrilegious: Choose Sigmarites or Ulricans; recognisers have Animosity toward its bearer (WFRP page 190). |
| 52–56 | Bewitched: 1d10: 1 minor Corruption source; 2–5 additional Quirk or Curse from page 56 with +40; 6–10 recognisers have Animosity toward the bearer. |
| 57–73 | Battle Tested: Those recognising and respecting its battle history treat the bearer as one Status tier higher, maximum Gold, for Intimidate, Leadership and Charm (WFRP page 49). |
| 74–80 | Bitterly Remembered: Recognisers of this group have Hatred toward its bearer (WFRP page 190). D10: 1 Fimir; 2 Dark Elves; 3 Dragons; 4 Daemons; 5–6 mortal followers of a particular Chaos God; 7–8 Vampires and Necromancers; 9-10 Dwarfs. |
| 81–89 | Heirloom: Its wealthy former owner’s family may pay for return and resent refusal to sell. |
| 90–96 | Sought: Its former owner and mercenary adventuring band seek it after finishing a commission. |
| 97–00 | Storied: Roll twice more. |

Recognition depends on historical knowledge. Trust may end hostility; a distinguished new bearer may rehabilitate the weapon’s reputation.

description:45c0d07607b2e0510bb2b677.name: Magical Ammunition Table
description:45c0d07607b2e0510bb2b677.text:

| 75–91 | Arrow of True Flight: +30 Ballistic Skill when fired. |
| 92–00 | Hail of Doom Arrow: Splits into 1d10 arrows; roll hit and Damage separately for each. Assign to the primary target or visible secondary targets within 5 feet of it. |

description:08c5b8e443006ad8cf54ef68.text:

| 2 | Human | Short |
| 3 | Human | Short |
| 4 | Human | Average |
| 5 | Human | Average |
| 6 | Elf | Average |
| 7 | Elf | Average |
| 8 | Dwarf | Tall |
| 9 | Dwarf | Tall |
| 10 | Halfling | Exceedingly Tall |

The GM decides fit. Mail allows some tolerance; plate requires matching proportions. A smaller wearer may use oversized armour at +1 Encumbrance per piece. A skilled smith, ideally trained in magic, may resize it without disrupting enchantments.

description:4984e8a224db4b370eb8fb4c.name: Magical Armour Qualities
description:4984e8a224db4b370eb8fb4c.text:

| 43–44 | Gifted Armour: Gromril or Ithilmar fitted to its recipient, potentially Human, Halfling or Ogre. Khazalid runes confirm the gift and return terms. |
| 45–51 | Alleviating Armour: For each Critical Wound suffered, the attacker rolls twice on the appropriate table and uses the lower result. |
| 52–58 | Seamless Armour: A full mail suit gains Impenetrable; a full plate suit loses Weakpoints. |
| 59–65 | Dragon Scale Armour: Protected locations reduce flame or heat Damage by 2 and ignore Ablaze Conditions an attack would inflict. |
| 66–76 | Armour of Glittering Silver: A full suit in sunlight or other strong light requires melee opponents to pass Average (+20) Agility at each Round’s start or gain one Blinded Condition. |
| 77–88 | Trickster’s Armour: A hit to a protected area is cancelled on 1d10 of 10. |
| 89–96 | Armour of Resilience: A full suit grants +5 Toughness. |
| 97–99 | Armour of Fortune: A hit to a protected area is cancelled on 1d10 of 9 or 10. |

Magical shields protect against attacks ignoring non-magical armour. Roll on Shield Quality for further abilities.

description:92720d7b1b740c45f3850aea.name: Scroll Table
description:92720d7b1b740c45f3850aea.text:
| D100 | Lore | Max CN | D100 | Lore | Max CN |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 01–03 | Petty | 0 | 74–81 | Light | 7 |
| 04–25 | Arcane | 1 | 82–89 | Shadows | 8 |
| 26–33 | Beasts | 2 | 90 | Hedgecraft | 0 |
| 34–41 | Death | 3 | 91–93 | Witchcraft | 9 |
| 42–49 | Fire | 4 | 94–96 | Daemonology | 10 |
| 50–57 | Heavens | 5 | 97–99 | Necromancy | 11 |
| 58–65 | Metal | 5 | 00 | Chaos Magic (any Chaos God) | 12 |
| 66–73 | Life | 6 |  |  |  |

Using a scroll takes an Action: brandish it, read its command and pass Challenging (+0) Language (Magick). Scrolls intended for non-Wizards instead require Hard (–20) Language in their written language; commands may be rendered phonetically. Success casts the spell and destroys the scroll. Failure does nothing; retry in later Rounds. Miscasts remain possible, but all scroll spells count as using ingredients (WFRP page 236).

The source lists Witchcraft scrolls as minor Corruption, then lists Daemonology, Necromancy, Witchcraft and Chaos Magic as moderate Corruption. This overlap remains unresolved.

description:5a519559554cfab83a02d44a.name: Shield Quality Table
description:5a519559554cfab83a02d44a.text:
| D100 | Ability |

description:08159d2804a1b65a59e4ef41.name: Battlefield Strength
description:08159d2804a1b65a59e4ef41.text:
Before battle, the GM assigns each Army Power from 0 to 100 based on relative size and strength. Use these comparisons as guidance.

|  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Characters’ Army | Ally Power | Foe Power | Examples |
| Insignificant | 30 | 70 | A provincial city’s defense against a Vampire Count and his undead legions. |
| Disadvantaged | 40 | 60 | A mercenary company against a Greenskin Waaagh! |
| Evenly Matched | 50 | 50 | Provincial armies facing each other in the open field. |
| Advantaged | 60 | 40 | A well-provisioned castle defending against a horde of unorganised Clanrats. |
| Overwhelming | 70 | 30 | An alliance of Humans and Dwarfs assaulting a Beastmen warcamp. |

description:9337c276f9e4e3490dc0c69f.name: Battlefield Power Modifiers
description:9337c276f9e4e3490dc0c69f.text:
Alternatively, start each Army at 30 Power and apply all relevant modifiers. Subtract 10 from both repeatedly until both lie within 0–100. A Power difference greater than 100 means the outcome is determined.

|  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Modifiers | Power Modifier | Examples |
| Badly Equipped | −10 | Light (Armour 1) or less, Improvised Weapons, Weapon +4 or less |
| Well Equipped | +10 | Heavy Armour (Armour 5), Blackpowder Weapons, Weapon +10 or higher |
| Includes Spellcasters | +10 | Wizards, Priests, Vampires |
| Includes Veteran Units | +10 | Melee or Ranged Skill at 45 or higher |
| Includes Elite Units | +20 | Melee or Ranged Skill at 60 or higher |
| Includes Small Units | −10 | Halflings, Snotlings |
| Includes Large Units | +10 | Ogres, Trolls, Horse Cavalry |
| Includes Enormous Units | +20 | Griffons, Wyverns |
| Includes Monstrous Units | +30 | Dragons, Giants |

description:556e372ef50ad434b567e9a9.name: Battle Endeavours
description:556e372ef50ad434b567e9a9.text: Between Adventures, Characters may undertake up to three pre-battle Endeavours within the time the GM allows. Resolve their Skill Tests directly or play scenes or adventures. Retry a failed Endeavour only with a different approach.

description:c87a0bb1baf8937b46af49bb.name: Infiltrate
description:c87a0bb1baf8937b46af49bb.text: Requires successful Scout. Make Combined Stealth and Perception, or Combined Entertain (Acting) and Perception to impersonate an enemy soldier; the GM sets Difficulty. Scout results may offer other approaches. Success grants +20 to Plan. Failure forces escape or capture. A different Species makes infiltration significantly harder.

description:10d6d301608403b95ff491dc.name: Inspiring Speech
description:10d6d301608403b95ff491dc.text: Test Leadership with Difficulty based on the Armies’ Power difference rounded to the nearest 10. Success grants +10 to the Army’s first Battle Round Power Test.

description:4bf655be32bbc2b1076b60d7.name: Muster Forces
description:4bf655be32bbc2b1076b60d7.text: Gather troops through payment, persuasion, bribery or intimidation; circumstances determine Skills and Difficulties. Success adds +5 Army Power; Astounding Success (+6) adds +10; Astounding Failure (−6) reduces Power by −10.

description:451c9bf69b0aaa50f95dd61e.name: Sabotage
description:451c9bf69b0aaa50f95dd61e.text: Requires successful Scout, whose findings determine sabotage options. Usually Test Stealth or Entertain (Acting), possibly during Infiltrate. Success reduces enemy Power by −5, or −10 on Astounding Success (+6). Failure requires fleeing or fighting out of camp.

description:f4ed929360841c0ca4715cbe.name: Scout
description:f4ed929360841c0ca4715cbe.text: Make Challenging (+0) Combined Ride and Perception. Success reveals enemy numbers, distance, troop types and Power, granting +10 to Plan. Failure gathers incorrect information or returns too late, giving no bonus. Astounding Failure (−6) may require escaping enemy scouts to avoid capture.

description:1b2026dcffb056266c2404fa.name: War Machines
description:1b2026dcffb056266c2404fa.text:
| Weapon | Price | Crew | Availability | Range***/ Reach | Damage | Qualities and Flaws |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Ballista | 75GC | 4 | Rare | 150 | +14 | Impale, Penetrating, Reload 2 |
| Battering Ram* | 10GC | 6 | Scarce | Average | +SB+10 | Siege |
| Helstorm Rocket Battery | 200GC | 4 | Exotic | 200 | +12 | Dangerous, Reload 5, Blast 15, Imprecise |
| Helblaster Volley Cannon | 300GC | 4 | Exotic | 100 | +14 | Blackpowder, Dangerous, Reload 5, Repeater 3, Blast 5 |
| Cannon | 120GC | 4 | Exotic | 120 | +20 | Blackpowder, Dangerous, Reload 3, Blast 3, Siege |
| Dwarf Flame Cannon | 200GC | 4 | Exotic | 60 | Special | Dangerous, Reload 3, Imprecise, Blast 5 |
| Mangonel Catapult | 60GC | 6 | Rare | 60 | +10 | Blast 5, Reload 4, Siege |
| Onager Catapult | 80GC | 6 | Rare | 100 | +12 | Blast 5, Reload, Siege |
| Trebuchet** | 40GC | 8 | Scarce | 150 | +14 | Blast 5, Reload 5, Siege |
| Mortar** | 100GC | 6 | Exotic | 200 | +20 | Blackpowder, Blast 5, Dangerous, Imprecise, Reload 2, Siege |

* Battering Rams damage only doors and gates; otherwise use Improvised Weapon. ** Trebuchets and Mortars cannot attack closer than Short Range. *** Ranged siege weapons cannot attack at Point Blank.

description:9fc23661df43bf365be1f709.name: Typical Barricades And Cover
description:9fc23661df43bf365be1f709.text:

| Door | 2 | 8 | Resistant |
| Reinforced Door | 5 | 15 | Resistant |
| Gate | 10 | 30 | Impervious |
| Wooden Wall | 6 | 15 | Resistant |
| Stone Wall | 12 | 40 | Impervious |

description:77954b605068750f89101cd4.name: Options: Environmental Factors
description:77954b605068750f89101cd4.text:
Optionally roll or choose an environmental factor for a Battle or Battle Round.

| 1d10 | Environmental Factor |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | Storm: Melee combatants smaller than Large suffer −10 Combat Tests and halve Movement. Ranged attackers and flying mounts suffer −20 Combat Tests; Stealth gains +20. Lore of Heavens Wizards gain +10 Casting and Channelling. |
| 2 | Traps: Each move requires Challenging (+0) Perception to avoid triggering a trap, then Challenging (+0) Dodge to avoid its effects. Traps inflict 8 Damage and appropriate Conditions: Entangled for bear traps or Prone in pits. Each activation lets nearby Characters attempt Hard (−20) Perception to avoid later traps. Capturing the enemy engineer’s trap plan neutralises all traps. |
| 3 | Siege Weapons: At each Round’s end, everyone passes Easy (+40) Dodge or suffers a Critical Wound. Defeating their crews ends this effect and allows using the weapons against the enemy. |
| 4 | Corrupting Influence: At each Battle Round’s end, everyone passes Challenging (+0) Endurance or gains 1 Corruption. The GM may make Easy (+40) Endurance using average troop Willpower, typically 35. Failure makes a nearby ally mutate and attack either side. |
| 5 | Toxic Cloud: Obscures like fog. At each Combat Round’s end, occupants pass Challenging (+0) Endurance or gain Poisoned. Ignition inflicts 3 Ablaze Conditions on everyone inside. |
| 6 | Rough Undergrowth: Halve Movement; Fumbles also cause Entangled. A blade user may clear it in a Cinematic Scene with successful Melee. |
| 7 | River: Those smaller than Large suffer −20 Combat Tests. Ending a turn in the river requires Challenging (+0) Strength to avoid being swept away. Controlling the bridge makes only the enemy cross the river. |
| 8 | Inferno: Moving requires Challenging (+0) Athletics to avoid 1 Ablaze Condition. Disable its source to extinguish it after 1 Battle Round. |
| 9 | Undeath: Each Army Power lost gives the enemy +1 Power. Defeat the necromancer to end this and remove all Power gained this way. |
| 10 | Fear: Army Power Tests suffer −10 while the enemy’s terrifying structure stands. |

description:83e55c87b64a9f23944fb901.name: New Endeavour: Recuperation
description:83e55c87b64a9f23944fb901.text: Make Very Hard (–30) Cool, potentially easier with good care. Success removes one chosen Psychology. Whether successful or not, during the next adventure you may reverse one Cool Test resisting Psychology.

description:7589ee33da662d03bf2684a6.text: Use Toughness for Language (Magick). Casting requires suitable meat within living costs; without it, lose Wounds equal to the spell’s CN. Ordinary meat does not protect against Miscasts. Esoteric ingredients cost 1 shilling per CN or may be acquired. The page separately charges CN Wounds when casting without a suitable ingredient; the GM must adjudicate this wording. These references do not automatically deduct Wounds or coins.

description:f03fa0074bb521d5b3768640.text: After successfully casting a Great Maw Lore spell, roll 1d10. On 10 or a result equal to or above the unmodified CN, recover that many Wounds. Use the unmodified CN despite Channelling or a Grimoire. Ingredients include bloody animal parts, unusual bile, marrow and cured fat. Healing is a play reference and is not applied automatically.

description:f2eb60457068d91d5b32fa44.name: Bonecrusher
description:f2eb60457068d91d5b32fa44.text: A Damage +4 magic missile ignores Armour Points but allows Toughness Bonus. If it causes a Critical Wound, add +20 to the severity roll on the relevant Critical Wound table. Casting requires chewing a mouthful of bones.

description:2928d8d9b1acc04303db816a.name: Bullgorger
description:2928d8d9b1acc04303db816a.text: Consume a mighty beast’s heart to grant the target +2 Strength Bonus for Damage and other appropriate feats of Strength for the duration. When it ends, the target must immediately eat a substantial meal or gain a Fatigued Condition. An unwilling target can reject the effect with a Difficult (−1 SL) Cool Test.

description:3fc43b88cc20c5ed855b763e.name: Braingobbler
description:3fc43b88cc20c5ed855b763e.text: After eating a whole head, including its brains, gain Fear 2 (WFRP p. 341). Anyone resisting this Fear who had a close relationship with the head’s former owner takes −20 on their Cool Tests.

description:42c81fe0ddb59ca060032909.name: Taste Death
description:42c81fe0ddb59ca060032909.text: Eating part of a corpse reveals approximately when and how it died, including the general weapon or cause, but no further detail or culprit. A death free of poison or disease is considered clean; custom then calls for consuming the remaining corpse.

description:0cf637af73632a95595d2b49.name: Trollguts
description:0cf637af73632a95595d2b49.text: Swallow a little Troll Bile or a similar substance to give the target Regeneration (WFRP p. 341). Ogres have no additional effect. Each non-Ogre who recovers Wounds this way must pass an Average (+2 SL) Endurance Test or develop mottled green or blue new flesh, especially on regrown limbs. This is not a mutation, though observers may mistake it for one.

description:18ca2e938e51040ca69ce7a2.name: The Maw
description:18ca2e938e51040ca69ce7a2.text: Consume most of a large beast to open a bottomless, toothed pit. Everyone in the area immediately Tests Challenging (+0 SL) Dodge. Success avoids falling but causes a Damage +8 hit, reduced by 1 per SL on that Test. Failure causes a Damage +10 hit to a random location and 3 Entangled Conditions, opposed by Strength 60; all 3 must be removed to escape. Each creature inside takes another Damage +10 hit to a random location at the end of each of its turns. When the spell ends, the pit disappears; anyone still inside suffers a Critical Wound to a random hit location.

description:163ff4434a26a848a405b18d.name: Feast of the Fallen
description:163ff4434a26a848a405b18d.text: Bathe a blade in a freshly slain foe’s blood. Chosen creatures in the area gain Vampiric (WFRP p. 343) for the duration, activating it by wounding enemies in melee without needing to bite; other healing still works. An unwilling creature can resist with a Difficult (−1 SL) Endurance Test. When the spell ends, non-Ogres who wounded an enemy in melee must pass Challenging (+0 SL) Cool or gain a Stunned Condition. If they wounded a creature with Infected or Diseased, Tests against those Traits’ harmful effects take −30.

description:7a8df8a2fa8946a12e03f714.name: Vice (Target)
description:7a8df8a2fa8946a12e03f714.text: Max: Willpower Bonus. Tests: Willpower to resist the chosen Vice. Each purchase gives a different Vice, such as Alcohol, Food, Narcotics or Pleasure. Encountering its target requires a Psychology Test (WFRP p. 190). Failure forces unhealthy indulgence instead of all other actions or duties, until insensible; gain one Fatigued Condition. At each later Round’s end, another Psychology Test can end this state. Fellowship Tests towards witnesses suffer −20. Each full day without indulgence adds a cumulative −20 to Psychology Tests until you indulge.

description:055c301b0a1b377c51ae0edd.name: Ogre Club
description:055c301b0a1b377c51ae0edd.text: Optional modifications (p. 30): metal plates grant Pummel, rusty spikes grant Penetrating, and scavenged blades grant Hack. Quality/Flaw editing is deferred; the creator selects none automatically. Price and Encumbrance already reflect Ogre size; do not double them. Availability applies in the Empire (p. 29). Average creatures can barely use these weapons; ask the GM (p. 28).

description:ca701fa298594e58d1ab65c2.name: Ironfist
description:ca701fa298594e58d1ab65c2.text: An Ironfist cannot be disarmed from an Ogre. Its hand remains usable for holding a weapon and simple actions (p. 30). Price and Encumbrance already reflect Ogre size; do not double them. Availability applies in the Empire (p. 29). Average creatures can barely use these weapons; ask the GM (p. 28).

description:1269f4568228895515bbd037.name: Big Ogre Club (2H)
description:1269f4568228895515bbd037.text: Optional modifications (p. 30): metal plates grant Pummel, rusty spikes grant Penetrating, and scavenged blades grant Hack. Quality/Flaw editing is deferred; the creator selects none automatically. Price and Encumbrance already reflect Ogre size; do not double them. Availability applies in the Empire (p. 29). Average creatures can barely use these weapons; ask the GM (p. 28).

description:3679c992af2981f2d5d2d780.name: Great Throwing Spear
description:3679c992af2981f2d5d2d780.text: Ogre Hunter javelin (p. 30). Price and Encumbrance already reflect Ogre size; do not double them. Availability applies in the Empire (p. 29). Average creatures can barely use these weapons; ask the GM (p. 28).

description:fdd062d46a4ec4c4231b46ea.name: Leadbelcher Gun (2H)
description:fdd062d46a4ec4c4231b46ea.text: Fires shot or cannonballs (p. 30). Inherent Blackpowder and Damaging Qualities follow core p. 303. Price and Encumbrance already reflect Ogre size; do not double them. Availability applies in the Empire (p. 29). Average creatures can barely use these weapons; ask the GM (p. 28).

description:9db4c4f6a37d2effe8bdbea0.name: Ogre Pistol
description:9db4c4f6a37d2effe8bdbea0.text: Uses standard blackpowder shot and powder. It also functions as a Hand Weapon and breaks only on a Fumbled attack (p. 30); this grants no separate weapon. Inherent Blackpowder and Damaging Qualities follow core p. 303. Price and Encumbrance already reflect Ogre size; do not double them. Availability applies in the Empire (p. 29). Average creatures can barely use these weapons; ask the GM (p. 28).

description:c47a9d21fb60266f0d9d2a25.name: Harpoon Launcher
description:c47a9d21fb60266f0d9d2a25.text: Use Ranged (Crossbow) or Ranged (Entangling), without penalty. The profile includes the rope; removing it gives range 60 and removes Entangle (p. 30). Price and Encumbrance already reflect Ogre size; do not double them. Availability applies in the Empire (p. 29). Average creatures can barely use these weapons; ask the GM (p. 28).

description:d8b2498db3fb3a26a677ce4a.name: Chain Trap
description:d8b2498db3fb3a26a677ce4a.text: Throw the chained jaws at prey, then reel the target in (p. 30). Price and Encumbrance already reflect Ogre size; do not double them. Availability applies in the Empire (p. 29). Average creatures can barely use these weapons; ask the GM (p. 28).

description:44606b3871dd7be81ffd79be.name: Face of the Wild
description:44606b3871dd7be81ffd79be.text: Spend 1 SL of gathered power to gain Fear (1) until your next turn.

description:07f890a01148dfd313e6e9a0.name: Talons of Ghur
description:07f890a01148dfd313e6e9a0.text: Until your next turn, spend gathered power to add +1 Damage per SL to an unarmed attack, up to Willpower Bonus SL. Choose after the Melee Test but before the GM announces its result.

description:09fcc23d999641543ad603a2.name: Thick Hide
description:09fcc23d999641543ad603a2.text: Spend 3 SL of gathered power: until your next turn, worn leather armour grants +1 AP at each location it covers.

description:a382fc6e6c509abfabe17c4b.name: Eyes of Death
description:a382fc6e6c509abfabe17c4b.text: Spend 1 SL of gathered power and choose a visible creature. The GM describes its remaining Wounds in relative terms.

description:e5f7e032761aa0f54732ccd6.name: Whispers of Doom
description:e5f7e032761aa0f54732ccd6.text: Spend 2 SL of gathered power to learn a creature’s Dooming if you dealt it at least 1 Wound within the last Willpower Bonus minutes.

description:9567806643f05d2105beb57d.name: Death’s Visage
description:9567806643f05d2105beb57d.text: Spend 3 SL of gathered power. For this round, you need no breath and ignore Fatigued, disease and Poisoned effects. Undead ignore you unless you directly attack them or they are intelligent enough to recognise the deception.

description:b86ac788e8e74a2c5893cb30.name: Brighten Blaze
description:b86ac788e8e74a2c5893cb30.text: Spend 1 SL of gathered power to intensify a visible non-magical fire within Willpower yards: a candle becomes torch-strength, a torch campfire-strength, and so on. Illumination increases; the GM may give nearby creatures one Ablaze Condition if the enlarged fire reaches them.

description:bebabf9c71eb702c3f6f61b0.name: Set Alight
description:bebabf9c71eb702c3f6f61b0.text: When a Melee attack hits, spend 2 SL of gathered power to give the opponent one Ablaze Condition.

description:aac7f491848d1e6431103718.name: Fervent Bellow
description:aac7f491848d1e6431103718.text: Shout encouragement and spend 3 SL of gathered power to remove one Broken Condition from one ally who hears you.

description:b4560ae42437cf764818eae4.name: Visions of Trauma
description:b4560ae42437cf764818eae4.text: Spend 1 SL of gathered power for +1 SL on a Dodge or Melee Test to evade or parry an attack.

description:92039467eac9c9fae531013d.name: Crackling Blade
description:92039467eac9c9fae531013d.text: Spend gathered power on a Melee attack with a metal weapon for +1 Damage per SL, up to Willpower Bonus SL. Choose after the Melee Test but before the GM announces its result.

description:490087f1ad3772d555c14a1e.name: Visions of Fortune
description:490087f1ad3772d555c14a1e.text: Spend 3 SL of gathered power and call advice to an ally who hears you. They gain +2 SL on one Test of their choice during their next turn. You cannot target yourself.

description:01e2e0a42ed1243d16607505.name: Reinforcement
description:01e2e0a42ed1243d16607505.text: Spend 1 SL of gathered power: worn metal armour grants +1 AP to each covered location until your next turn.

description:585461045241486befe926c4.name: Heart of Iron
description:585461045241486befe926c4.text: When you receive a Critical Wound, spend 2 SL of gathered power. The attacker rolls twice on the relevant Critical Wound chart and uses the less harmful result.

description:51f96a05b689d82e623ef2d0.name: Quicksilver Blade
description:51f96a05b689d82e623ef2d0.text: Spend 3 SL of gathered power on a metal weapon you hold. For this Round, its Melee attacks count as Chamon spells and gain the Fifth Edition core Lore of Metal effects: ignore metal armour AP and add Damage equal to the metal armour AP on the struck location.

description:40e6263f7c1fa96345a905d1.name: Staunch
description:40e6263f7c1fa96345a905d1.text: Spend 1 SL of gathered power to remove every Fatigued and Bleeding Condition you have.

description:97de757584e807054bc9385f.name: Invigorate
description:97de757584e807054bc9385f.text: As an Action, spend 2 SL of gathered power and touch a creature. Until your next turn, it gains +1 SL on Strength- or Toughness-based Tests and automatically passes Tests against disease or poison effects.

description:a1a3be313ff1b6adb571a6fd.name: Regenerate
description:a1a3be313ff1b6adb571a6fd.text: At your turn’s start, spend 3 SL of gathered power to gain the Fifth Edition core Regeneration Trait until the next Round starts.

description:8bdac602635d1027f989eb2b.name: Brighteyes
description:8bdac602635d1027f989eb2b.text: Spend 1 SL of gathered power to gain Dark Vision and immunity to Blinded until your next turn begins. Existing Blinded Conditions are suppressed, then resume when this ends.

description:1e33cee4c31f8d7a50a37034.name: Purging Light
description:1e33cee4c31f8d7a50a37034.text: Spend 2 SL of gathered power on a held melee weapon or one piece of ammunition. Until your next turn, a target it hits must pass a Challenging (+0 SL) Endurance Test or gain one Blinded Condition. A Daemonic target also suffers +3 Damage.

description:ea257d507c28b2cd118937f4.name: Perfection of the Self
description:ea257d507c28b2cd118937f4.text: Spend 3 SL of gathered power to ignore your Diseases, Poisons, Critical Wounds and Mutations until your next turn. Hysh temporarily replaces missing limbs for this duration.

description:9aecdc25a3c6c7ffd393d6e7.name: Ulgu’s Touch
description:9aecdc25a3c6c7ffd393d6e7.text: Spend 1 SL of gathered power. On Stealth Tests this Round, add up to Willpower Bonus SL after rolling but before the GM announces the result.

description:24573f94d8772c46921a0d71.name: Not Your Problem
description:24573f94d8772c46921a0d71.text: Spend 2 SL of gathered power. A hostile enemy attacks another viable target on its next turn if at least one is available.

description:d83acaf3918dcc55fd5a6585.name: A Passing Shadow
description:d83acaf3918dcc55fd5a6585.text: Spend 3 SL of gathered power to escape existing restraints. Attempts to grab, hold or otherwise stop your movement fail; difficult terrain does not hinder you, and you can pass barred windows and other narrow gaps.

description:092bc873782528edc107e03b.name: Priest of Solkan
description:092bc873782528edc107e03b.text: Recommended mainly for NPCs or a suitable party; a restrained priest who works with the group is permitted (p. 53). Any Sin or Corruption points prevent Solkan from granting Blessings or Miracles (p. 55).

description:050eaada4a290f24677758de.name: Priestess of Rhya
description:050eaada4a290f24677758de.text: Priests may be male. Rhya permits neither Warrior Priests nor Witch Hunters (p. 73).

description:51d96e89caa374c027254872.name: Enterprise Events
description:51d96e89caa374c027254872.text:
Between adventures, an Enterprise investor may replace their normal Events roll (WFRP page 193) with this table before choosing Endeavours. Only one investor per Enterprise may do so in a downtime phase; an Enterprise receives at most one Event.

| d100 | Event | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 01–02 | Looming Bankruptcy | Lose the latest Expansion’s benefits but retain its increased Debt and Interest; repay all Debt to restore them. Without an Expansion, close the business, dismiss staff and sell Trappings; Debt remains. The GM may allow an adventure to avert failure. |
| 03–05 | Recession | No Character may use this Enterprise for Earning or Income Endeavours until the next adventure ends. |
| 06–08 | Shoplifter Strikes | The most valuable portable Trapping is stolen; recover it during the next adventure or accept the loss. |
| 09–10 | Interest Inflation | Double Interest Payments until all Debt is repaid. |
| 11–13 | Trapping Degrades | The GM degrades a Trapping: item Flaw, lost animal Trained Skill or employee Condition. Severe effects are usually temporary, milder ones persistent; an already degraded item may be destroyed or lost. |
| 14–16 | New Competition | Undertake at least one Income Endeavour with it in this batch, receiving only 50% of normal income. The rival remains an ongoing threat. |
| 17–20 | Forced to Diversify | The GM blocks the most-used Source of Income for this batch of Endeavours; other sources remain usable. |
| 21–23 | The Dreaded Auditors | Spend an Endeavour helping auditors or pay 10% of Start-Up Costs or latest Expansion Costs, whichever is higher. |
| 24–26 | Gimme a Discount | Decide whether to discount now; resolve consequences next adventure. Refusal causes public slander; acceptance may prompt other demands and reduce Income Statuses. |
| 27–30 | I Need a Holiday | You cannot choose Income in the next batch of Endeavours; other investors may still use the Enterprise for Income. |
| 31–33 | Conservative Investments | No Character can acquire an Expansion Creditor during the next batch of Endeavours. |
| 34–36 | The Grind | If possible, choose Income before the next adventure; no other effect. |
| 37–39 | I Quit! | An NPC employee, if present, leaves; replace them by the next adventure’s start. |
| 40–41 | New Creditor | The current Creditor transfers the Debt to a new Creditor. |
| 42–44 | Closed for Refurbishment | No Income from the Enterprise during the next batch. Afterwards improved accommodation may grant GM-chosen Skill Test bonuses. |
| 45–48 | Creditor Visits | Before the next adventure, repay Debt (page 8) without spending an Endeavour. |
| 49–51 | New Hire | Gain an NPC employee who requires substantial training and supervision. |
| 52–54 | Breakup Opportunity | If Expanded, you may surrender the latest Expansion’s Trappings and benefits to clear all Debt. Later Expansion remains possible. |
| 55–57 | Alternate Event 1 | Use the specific Enterprise template’s Alternate Event 1. |
| 58–60 | Alternate Event 2 | Use the specific Enterprise template’s Alternate Event 2. |
| 61–63 | Business as Usual | No special effect. |
| 64–66 | Co-Ownership | If accepted, the co-owner pays half the outstanding Debt; you must accommodate their development ideas. |
| 67–69 | Upgraded Trapping | The GM improves a Trapping: item Quality, animal Trained Skill, employee Skill, or appropriate removal of a Flaw or Condition. |
| 70–72 | Merger Opportunity | Investors may immediately Expand, paying normal costs but no Endeavour, even while indebted. Creditor funding adds to current Debt. Use the new Expanded Interest rate until all Debt is repaid. |
| 73–75 | Desperate Customer | Choose a Source of Income; increase its effective Status number by 1 until the next adventure starts. |
| 76–78 | In the Black | No additional effect. |
| 79–81 | Temporary Expansion | Gain the next Expansion level’s benefits until the next adventure ends, without Expansion Costs or changed Interest. |
| 82–85 | Taking Care of Itself | Immediately take an Income Endeavour with the Enterprise; it does not count against the pre-adventure maximum. |
| 86–88 | Innovation | Gain a Source of Income agreed with the GM, including required Trappings and effects. Usually match the second-highest existing effective Status and use a different Earning Skill. |
| 89–91 | Rolling Profits | Choose a Source of Income and permanently increase its effective Status number by 1. |
| 92–94 | New Trapping | Gain either a duplicate Trapping or a new one worth no more than Start-Up Costs or latest Expansion Costs, whichever is higher. |
| 95–97 | Unexpected Generosity | Skip this downtime’s Interest Payment. |
| 98–100 | Offer to Buy-Out | If all investors accept, surrender Enterprise benefits, clear Debt and split wealth equal to double Start-Up Costs or double latest Expansion Costs, whichever is higher. |

description:58de719d175506089d0302dc.name: Example Expansion Table
description:58de719d175506089d0302dc.text:
| Level | Cost | Interest | New Trappings | Effects |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2 | 10/- | 1/6 | Two Apprentices | Apprentices grant +10 Trade, make deliveries and tend the business during your absence. |
| 3 | 10 GC | 10/- | Former Apprentices become Artisans, plus either Rented Workspace or another Source of Income. | Artisans grant +20 Trade. Add one Source of Income: Rented Workspace (Haggle, Silver 1), a New Workshop (another chosen Trade Skill), Dedicated Storefront (Status Silver 2), or similar. |
| 4 | 20 GC | 1GC | Guildhall, many Apprentices, etc. | Add another Source of Income; the Workshop becomes a Guildhall. |

description:44764bc3147e08cbea5094f5.name: Looting Armour
description:44764bc3147e08cbea5094f5.text:
The GM may decide whether found armour fits, considering Species and body size. If uncertain, roll on this table.

| D10 Roll | Leather & Soft Kit | Brigandine and Chainmail | Plate |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1-2 | Suitable Fit | Suitable Fit | Suitable Fit |
| 3-4 | Suitable Fit | Suitable Fit | Poor Fit |
| 5-6 | Suitable Fit | Poor Fit | Poor Fit |
| 7-8 | Poor Fit | Poor Fit | Won't Fit |
| 9-10 | Won't Fit | Won't Fit | Won't Fit |

description:db031673c484da07c802dccb.name: Repairing Armour as an Endeavour
description:db031673c484da07c802dccb.text: With suitable tools, and a forge or workshop for plate, spend a downtime Endeavour and make one Average (+20) Trade Test. Each SL repairs 1 AP.

description:119f4f95b70750b08291de71.name: Repairing Armour With the Trade Skill
description:119f4f95b70750b08291de71.text:
Use the listed Trade Skill and required facilities. Make an Extended Challenging (+0) Trade Test once per hour; the second table gives SL needed to restore 1 AP to one location.

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Type of Armour | Trade Skill Used for Repairs |
| Leather Armour or Brigandine | Trade (Tailor) — Trade Tools needed |
| Chainmail | Trade (Smith) — Trade Tools needed |
| Plate | Trade (Smith) — Trade Tools and Forge or Workshop needed |
|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Type of Armour | SL Needed to Repair 1 AP |
| Leather | 5 |
| Brigandine | 7 |
| Chainmail or Reinforced Soft Kit | 10 |
| Plate | 15 |

description:6cae6b530e3c0260cb431424.name: Impenetrable
description:6cae6b530e3c0260cb431424.text: Ignore Critical Wounds from attacks whose to-hit roll is odd, including rolls such as 11 or 33.

description:661c4243172cf8f30cddb36a.name: Overcoat
description:661c4243172cf8f30cddb36a.text: Brigandine and Plate Breastplates may be layered over Leather or Mail armour.

description:2ea9190c01445603c6ed3fdd.name: Partial
description:2ea9190c01445603c6ed3fdd.text: Ignore this armour's AP when the attacker rolls an even Hit Location result or scores a Critical Hit.

description:3c025e0fae46faa1af7aa849.name: Reinforced
description:3c025e0fae46faa1af7aa849.text: A reinforcing Soft Kit worn beneath plate removes that plate's Weakpoints Flaw.

description:3e380d7bc0e116848d60a8ea.name: Requires Kit
description:3e380d7bc0e116848d60a8ea.text: Wearing this armour requires a Soft Kit underneath.

description:ad084bc097ec78190b9f9588.name: Visor
description:ad084bc097ec78190b9f9588.text: Opening or closing a visor costs an Action. Closed: use the helmet's normal profile. Open: lose its design-specific abilities, gain Partial, and apply the printed −10% to Perception Tests.

description:de5722058c80f9be45d67605.name: Weakpoints
description:de5722058c80f9be45d67605.text: A Critical scored with an Impale weapon bypasses this armour's AP.

description:4e3549cc2d7e0cfed967b912.name: Boiled Leather
description:4e3549cc2d7e0cfed967b912.text:

description:c573e9d5d007da8146195b20.text:
