description:b568c4cedc561675420ca866.name: Goodwill
description:b568c4cedc561675420ca866.text: CN: 0 Range: You Target: AoE (Fellowship Bonus yards) Duration: Willpower Bonus Rounds. Fellowship Tests in the area gain +10. Animosity and Hatred have no effect there.

description:8f16b2573bff8386c8ef036a.name: Mirkride
description:8f16b2573bff8386c8ef036a.text: CN: 0 Range: You Target: You Duration: Willpower Bonus minutes. Your spirit enters the Hedge, retaining its Characteristics, Skills and Talents. It can see the physical world, pass non-magical barriers, and is invisible and silent to physical beings and immune to non-magical Damage. It cannot handle physical objects, but can cast spells affecting them. It can see and interact with invisible, spirit, ethereal and Daemonic creatures. Your body stays immobile, insensate and Prone. The spell’s end returns you to it; touching your body also ends the spell. If your body dies during the spell, your spirit wanders forever.

description:a723fc2f5b9ec470b666e38e.name: Nepenthe
description:a723fc2f5b9ec470b666e38e.text: CN: 0 Range: Touch Target: Special Duration: The drink lasts Willpower Bonus hours; its effects are permanent. You need a cup or other drinking vessel to collect the conjured silver liquid. Drinking it permanently erases everything the drinker knows about one individual they choose.

description:4756b038c96dde5d51bb0f0f.name: Nostrum
description:4756b038c96dde5d51bb0f0f.text: CN: 0 Range: Touch Target: Special Duration: Willpower Bonus hours. Enchant a prepared draught. Drinking it before the spell expires restores Wounds equal to your Willpower Bonus and cures one disease you choose, plus one further disease per +2 SL on the Casting Test.

description:6609742534165ffbeb0a4aad.name: Part the Branches
description:6609742534165ffbeb0a4aad.text: CN: 0 Range: You Target: You Duration: Willpower minutes. You can see invisible creatures, spirits and Daemons in the spirit world.

description:03ecb48fac21b3d2ec40aba2.name: Protective Charm
description:03ecb48fac21b3d2ec40aba2.text: CN: 0 Range: Touch Target: Special Duration: Willpower Bonus days. Enchant a small charm, such as jewellery or a pocket trinket. Its bearer gains Magic Resistance; an existing Magic Resistance Talent receives no benefit.

description:f6b2f8869eedbb1d9616a167.name: Badger — familiar starting choices
description:f6b2f8869eedbb1d9616a167.text: Skills: Cool, Endurance, Intuition, Outdoor Survival, Perception, Swim Talents: Acute Sense (Smell), Second Sight, Sixth Sense Creature Traits: Armour 1, Belligerent, Bestial, Hardy, Night Vision, Size (Little), Skittish, Trained (Broken, Magic), Weapon+4

description:39047928943db4c4a5d869b1.name: Cat — familiar starting choices
description:39047928943db4c4a5d869b1.text: Skills: Athletics, Climb, Dodge, Outdoor Survival, Perception, Stealth (Rural or Urban) Talents: Luck, Scale Sheer Surface, Second Sight Creature Traits: Bestial, Night Vision, Size (Little), Skittish, Stealthy, Stride, Trained (Broken, Magic), Weapon+3

description:5411681a52c70ae5efdc9c15.name: Crow — familiar starting choices
description:5411681a52c70ae5efdc9c15.text: Skills: Gossip, Intuition, Perception, Language (Barnyard or Wild), Navigation, Outdoor Survival Talents: Magical Sense, Sixth Sense, Super Numerate Creature Traits: Bestial, Flight 80, Size (Little), Skittish, Trained (Broken, Magic), Weapon+2

description:0056ec4b23d126ca040cd3d9.name: Fox — familiar starting choices
description:0056ec4b23d126ca040cd3d9.text: Skills: Navigation, Perception, Outdoor Survival, Stealth (Rural), Swim, Track Talents: Luck, Magical Sense, Orientation Creature Traits: Bestial, Night Vision, Size (Little), Skittish, Stride, Tracker, Trained (Broken, Magic), Weapon+3

description:a02bfb6bc80c180d7ef40cbd.name: Owl — familiar starting choices
description:a02bfb6bc80c180d7ef40cbd.text: Skills: Dodge, Intuition, Outdoor Survival, Perception, Stealth (Rural), Track Talents: Acute Sense (Sight), Luck, Sixth Sense Creature Traits: Bestial, Flight 60, Night Vision, Size (Little), Skittish, Stealthy, Trained (Broken, Magic), Weapon+3

description:f0fb1abde952c4be4aa63ea4.name: Stoat — familiar starting choices
description:f0fb1abde952c4be4aa63ea4.text: Skills: Climb, Dodge, Outdoor Survival, Perception, Stealth (Rural), Swim Talents: Magical Sense, Rover, Second Sight Creature Traits: Bestial, Bite+2, Night Vision, Size (Little), Skittish, Stealthy, Trained (Broken, Magic), Weapon+2

description:060de1456cb0c837540d82dc.name: Spirit-Bonding Ritual
description:060de1456cb0c837540d82dc.text: CN: 30 Type: Any Lore Learning XP: 150. Requires a magically gifted animal that has been broken or befriended through an Animal Training Endeavour and attuned to your spirit for at least 1 week. No sacrifice is required, but its death may cause trauma (Corruption & Death, p. 81). Failure removes the animal’s Trained (Magic) Trait. Repeating the ritual requires another week of attunement.

description:2f1b092cf75b5ade5cd4aad7.name: Animal Telepathy
description:2f1b092cf75b5ade5cd4aad7.text: Caster and spirit-bonded familiar may initiate silent, non-verbal communication within 4 yards. Complexity is limited by the animal's Intelligence.

description:0db191662d351b11abc23156.name: Invisibility
description:0db191662d351b11abc23156.text: Once daily, the familiar becomes nearly invisible for its Willpower in hours; this cannot end early. Spotting it requires Very Hard (−30) Perception. While it hides, only observers with Magical Sense can spot it.

description:e24190e367c449db39866dad.name: Messenger
description:e24190e367c449db39866dad.text: The familiar can carry messages up to its Intelligence in miles away, following complex instructions without an Intelligence Test even beyond 4 yards from its caster. Unexplored routes may cause delay or danger. Use a tied-on letter, or speech if it has the appropriate Language Skill.

description:885e33dce22049136e941ca8.name: Sensory Sharing
description:885e33dce22049136e941ca8.text: The caster uses the bonded familiar's sight, hearing and smell at a range in miles equal to the lower of their Willpower scores. This does not permit casting from the animal or extend Animal Telepathy beyond 4 yards.

description:f43371cb3532bdfb3a68d689.name: A Deal’s a Deal
description:f43371cb3532bdfb3a68d689.text: After a successful Haggle Test, thank Handrich and shake hands to add +2 SL to that Test, increased by 1 per +2 SL on the Pray Test invoking this Miracle. The other negotiator also forms a favourable impression of you.

description:b87c384ecae5e2a73dd46c0f.name: Carry My Burdens
description:b87c384ecae5e2a73dd46c0f.text: Once delivery of goods has been agreed, pass an Animal Training Test to make the target serve as your pack animal, regardless of its usual aggression or wildness. It carries whatever you require during the journey but neither attacks nor obeys other commands. It returns to its wild state on arrival. Only one creature can be affected at once.

description:c9c4bce2c04789d9ba8fa5ec.name: Shake On It
description:c9c4bce2c04789d9ba8fa5ec.text: Seal a deal with a handshake. The target cannot oppose its terms for at least Fellowship Bonus Rounds. To contest them, they must beat your SL on an Average (+2 SL) Cool Test; success permits refusing one required action, and each additional 2 SL permits one action against the deal. You sense any breach. Breaking it yourself while the Miracle lasts gives you +1 Sin point.

description:109179b726689340b4166cf9.name: Supply and Demand
description:109179b726689340b4166cf9.text: First locate a buyer or seller of particular goods with Difficult (−1 SL) Gossip. Then alter those goods’ Availability by one level to change their Bartering Ratio (WFRP p. 291). Their apparent supply increases or decreases; goods you possess are unaffected.

description:5d8adebfdd7afa81ca64c9be.name: Trickle Down
description:5d8adebfdd7afa81ca64c9be.text: Give a gold coin and promise future wealth while addressing people below your Status. A successful Charm Test gains +1 SL per SL on the Pray Test invoking the Miracle.

description:e0059b89f8896ab8f629ecde.name: Twist of Fortune
description:e0059b89f8896ab8f629ecde.text: You may spend 1 of the target’s Fortune points as your own. They can contest your SL with a Challenging (+0 SL) Fellowship Test: beating you preserves their point; beating you by +4 SL also lets them spend 1 of yours as their own. A transferred point must be spent before that session ends; it returns to its original owner at the next session’s start.

description:7479c92096c0b1016f8b2784.name: Absolute Purity
description:7479c92096c0b1016f8b2784.text: Within Fellowship Bonus yards, each creature with Undead, Daemon or Spellcaster, any Sin or Corruption points, or Arcane Magic, Chaos Magic or Petty Magic takes 1d10 Wounds ignoring Toughness and AP. Allies and bystanders are included.

description:8f11434a027842b24279e075.name: Fist of Vengeance
description:8f11434a027842b24279e075.text: The target takes 1d10 + Willpower Bonus Damage, ignoring AP.

description:387a8ea0023eb4b8159e20f6.name: Flaming Blade
description:387a8ea0023eb4b8159e20f6.text: If you wield a sword, it becomes Magical and gains +6 Damage. Each creature it strikes gains +1 Ablaze Condition.

description:efa57e80851095b2a275debe.name: Fury of the Righteous Sun
description:efa57e80851095b2a275debe.text: Everyone within Fellowship Bonus yards gains Blinded Conditions equal to your Fellowship Bonus and is hit by a Damage +2 magic missile.

description:2dbfcfe07047aeab1e6056a0.name: Light of Stasis
description:2dbfcfe07047aeab1e6056a0.text: All targets in the area enter stasis for the duration and cannot move or act. Time-dependent events, including falls, missiles, injuries and Conditions, pause until the Miracle ends.

description:dac6441b502e57e9e32aa21d.name: Still the Winds
description:dac6441b502e57e9e32aa21d.text: For the duration, all magic within Fellowship Bonus yards is dispelled, magic items lose their magical properties temporarily, and Channelling and Casting Tests automatically fail. Second Sight shows inert Winds in the area.

description:06681f9a14879236d9f14e1f.name: Dagger of the Art
description:06681f9a14879236d9f14e1f.text: Transform a stick no longer than eight inches into a dagger with the Magical Quality. Against creatures with Ethereal or Corruption, its Damage is SB + 8. After the duration expires, a Challenging (+0 SL) Channelling Test each round maintains it.

description:75ef014070586e40fb40032b.name: Fellstave
description:75ef014070586e40fb40032b.text: When learning this spell, choose Beastmen (including Minotaurs and Centigors, excluding Skaven), Daemons, Orcs and Goblins, Ogres, Fimir, Trolls, or Undead; the GM may allow other types. Each further purchase costs the normal new-spell XP and selects another type. Whittle a wooden post at least three feet long and four inches across, carve warding symbols, and drive it into the ground before casting. For one month, matching creatures within 100 yards must pass Challenging (+0 SL) Cool or gain a Broken Condition. After recovering, they Test Challenging (+0 SL) Intuition; success identifies the Fellstave as the source of their magical panic.

description:38f0e045b312fd68e688a564.name: Invigorate
description:38f0e045b312fd68e688a564.text: The target ignores all Fatigued Conditions for the duration.

description:a038a2fb0453e8f879d7f3a0.name: Lovelock
description:a038a2fb0453e8f879d7f3a0.text: Collect the honey produced during the incantation in a cup or other drinking vessel. Anyone drinking this philtre falls in love with the first person they find romantically appealing, if there is one.

description:b13878c8f9f70565bec3300d.name: Protection Pouch
description:b13878c8f9f70565bec3300d.text: Requires a small pouch made from a small animal’s body, such as a bat or shrew. The spell grows purple herbs to place inside it. Wearing the filled pouch around the neck gives +1 SL to Cool Tests resisting supernatural effects, including Fear or Terror from Undead or Daemons, and +10 to Endurance Tests against disease or Poisoned Conditions.

description:88d525600c990fe1a8047560.name: Sightstep
description:88d525600c990fe1a8047560.text: Magical Sense detects nothing unusual about you, and Stealth Tests to hide from Daemons, spirits and ethereal creatures gain +2 SL. While this concealment lasts, you cannot cast, dispel or channel.

description:e37b8d744d1149aaa75b7a8d.name: Silvertide
description:e37b8d744d1149aaa75b7a8d.text: Over the duration, you find a total of 2d10 pennies in overlooked places.

description:a3c86d6b5f8bb4e85b0e60e1.name: The Ousting
description:a3c86d6b5f8bb4e85b0e60e1.text: One creature in range with Ethereal or Daemonic must pass Challenging (+0 SL) Willpower or lose Wounds equal to your Willpower Bonus. If reduced to 0 Wounds or fewer, it is banished from the physical world and cannot return for the duration.

description:2b174b5321de3454e9ff3d6d.name: Wyrd Ward
description:2b174b5321de3454e9ff3d6d.text: Touch the target, then win an Opposed Willpower Test. For the duration, their Language (Magick) and Channelling Tests to cast Witchcraft, Necromancy, Daemonology or any Chaos Lore spell take −2 SL.

description:d3b343eb3289109c5ab2fa42.name: Rhya’s Abundance
description:d3b343eb3289109c5ab2fa42.text: Touch up to one barrel, crate or basket of stored food or uncooked ingredients each round. Its contents double, become fresh, and lose mould, vermin, insects and other spoilage.

description:52984c1786a4567c420ecaa3.name: Rhya’s Demand
description:52984c1786a4567c420ecaa3.text: Humanoids within Fellowship Bonus yards who have not sacrificed since the last spring equinox to Rhya, or a nature deity or powerful nature spirit accepted by her cult, lose 1 Wound +1 per SL and gain a Fatigued Condition. Examples of accepted patrons include Isha and Taal. If at least five people are affected, the ground within Fellowship yards becomes infertile for d10 years.

description:1749a3248ca75b3ed0cb5a54.name: Rhya’s Dominion
description:1749a3248ca75b3ed0cb5a54.text: Focus on a natural feature that could house a spirit. On success, its spirit appears and performs one task for Rhya. It may interpret instructions literally, and cannot fulfil requests that breach Rhya’s strictures.

description:0dd77a000cfd6b34f64a59ff.name: Rhya’s Flock
description:0dd77a000cfd6b34f64a59ff.text: Control a flock, herd or pack of domesticated animals, sense their moods and share all their senses. You may calm or agitate them and direct actions within their natural behaviour, including sleeping, stampeding or attacking.

description:a552db8f626a260b4f8dc459.name: Rhya’s Taming
description:a552db8f626a260b4f8dc459.text: Pass Average (+2 SL) Charm Animal to tame an uncorrupted wild animal of Large Size or smaller. It becomes docile towards Humans, Elves honouring Isha and similar allies, growing more compliant per SL. It will not willingly leave its natural territory.

description:947ccff7ee377991e7da0b02.name: Rhya’s Rage
description:947ccff7ee377991e7da0b02.text: Only usable while defending children or an inhabited home or farmstead. Gain Immunity to Psychology, Painless, and +2 SL on Melee, Strength and Toughness Tests.

description:d7c1e14f82d96de22a04e997.name: Hedgecraft Ingredients
description:d7c1e14f82d96de22a04e997.text: Costs 5 brass pennies (p. 6). Quantity, Encumbrance and Availability are unspecified, so a purchase records ingredients without a fixed number of spell uses. Hedgecraft casting requires them. Foraging and consumption remain deferred.

description:bd72e7be773941acc92f973f.name: Nameless Summons Table
description:bd72e7be773941acc92f973f.text:
| Result | Entity | Attitude | Suitable Gift |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| –5 or worse | A greater daemon’s forelimb drags you into its home realm. | Hostile | Your flesh, blood and soul. |
| –4 to –0 | A Lesser Daemon (WFRP page 256), Cairn Wraith, Tomb Banshee or comparable powerful spirit (pages 329–330). | Hostile | Immediately sacrifice 1d10 living sentient creatures. |
| +0 to +4 | A Lesser Daemon or powerful spirit, as above. | Neutral | Sacrifice one living sentient creature. |
| +5 to +9 | A Lesser Daemon or powerful spirit, as above. | Favourable | Promise a future sacrifice or great service. |
| +10 or better | A Greater Daemon willing to converse. | Neutral if its demands are met; otherwise Hostile. | Promise a great future service, such as founding its cult, and your essence upon death. |

The spell lasts indefinitely while the entity stays in the prepared circle, at most Willpower Bonus Yards wide. Upon leaving, it lasts up to the entity’s Willpower Bonus Rounds, minimum 1; the entity then returns to its origin.

description:c26f5e53a385bc4f27036be4.name: Badwill
description:c26f5e53a385bc4f27036be4.text:
Fellowship Tests in the area take −10, and Prejudice becomes Hatred. You may exempt yourself. The effect may attract malicious spirits.

Blood and Bramble p. 6: Hedgecraft spells require ingredients. A successful Lore (Herbalism) foraging roll provides 1 + SL ingredients; the printed purchase price is 5 brass pennies. Foraging and ingredient consumption are campaign references, not character-creation grants.

description:c02f9432255e79eff0f2a2a0.name: Bonesetter
description:c02f9432255e79eff0f2a2a0.text:
Hold the broken limb while the patient bites prepared bark and leather. Within one week of a Broken Bone injury (Fourth Edition core p. 179), reduce its healing time by 1d10 days plus another 1d10 per SL on the Casting Test, to a minimum of one day. Each broken bone can benefit only once.

Blood and Bramble p. 6: Hedgecraft spells require ingredients. A successful Lore (Herbalism) foraging roll provides 1 + SL ingredients; the printed purchase price is 5 brass pennies. Foraging and ingredient consumption are campaign references, not character-creation grants.

description:7854a0cea2a68ed1853eec0b.name: Cleanslate
description:7854a0cea2a68ed1853eec0b.text:
Immerse the target in running water or douse them with clean spring water. Resolve a Dispel attempt (Fourth Edition core p. 237) as though all required SL were achieved in one round. This removes most harmful magic, but excludes effects from worn or carried items, the items themselves, and non-magical consequences of magic such as Ablaze. Powerful curses may need further ingredients or trials; casting reveals these requirements.

Blood and Bramble p. 6: Hedgecraft spells require ingredients. A successful Lore (Herbalism) foraging roll provides 1 + SL ingredients; the printed purchase price is 5 brass pennies. Foraging and ingredient consumption are campaign references, not character-creation grants.

description:de8474b3a1da8b6155b11a57.name: Fertilise
description:de8474b3a1da8b6155b11a57.text:
Invoke the earth’s spirits and relieve yourself at the field’s four corners. Next season’s harvest will be at least average for that field despite weather, pests, poor soil or similar problems. The customary fee is one twentieth of its yield.

Blood and Bramble p. 6: Hedgecraft spells require ingredients. A successful Lore (Herbalism) foraging roll provides 1 + SL ingredients; the printed purchase price is 5 brass pennies. Foraging and ingredient consumption are campaign references, not character-creation grants.

description:11d11bdbc47f9cbdec5a4af3.name: Fetterfetch
description:11d11bdbc47f9cbdec5a4af3.text:
Enchant a dowsing instrument for a spirit you can name. Anyone can use it to find that spirit’s fetter: a nature spirit’s home, or a ghost’s remains, valued object or connected person. Following it requires an Extended Difficult (−1 SL) Navigate Test, one Test per hour, needing 5–15 SL according to distance, concealment and deliberate obstruction. Destroying a fetter usually banishes a spirit or releases a ghost, but killing a loved one may transfer the ghost’s bond to the killer. Resolving unfinished business or communicating for it may instead release it; an unwilling or hostile ghost can resist such efforts. The GM should give a ghost Regenerate while it defends its fetter.

Blood and Bramble p. 6: Hedgecraft spells require ingredients. A successful Lore (Herbalism) foraging roll provides 1 + SL ingredients; the printed purchase price is 5 brass pennies. Foraging and ingredient consumption are campaign references, not character-creation grants.

description:1e307926ce4703f62f257f06.name: Geistbane
description:1e307926ce4703f62f257f06.text:
Enchant a prepared oil-and-herb mixture. Applied to house entrances, it requires spirits to pass Hard (−2 SL) Willpower to enter. Applied to a weapon, it counts as magical against spirits, ghosts and Undead requiring magical attacks. Against Undead vulnerable to normal weapons, or on an already magical weapon, it instead grants Damaging against those creatures. Harming a living creature with the weapon ends the enchantment.

Blood and Bramble p. 6: Hedgecraft spells require ingredients. A successful Lore (Herbalism) foraging roll provides 1 + SL ingredients; the printed purchase price is 5 brass pennies. Foraging and ingredient consumption are campaign references, not character-creation grants.

description:c86ad387210998754e402394.name: Kindle
description:c86ad387210998754e402394.text:
Light gathered kindling. While fuel remains and the spell lasts, ordinary means cannot extinguish the fire. Endurance Tests against cold gain +20. Food cooked on it cannot burn, and rancid or poisoned ingredients become safe to eat.

Blood and Bramble p. 6: Hedgecraft spells require ingredients. A successful Lore (Herbalism) foraging roll provides 1 + SL ingredients; the printed purchase price is 5 brass pennies. Foraging and ingredient consumption are campaign references, not character-creation grants.

description:f28c60204154f88557387b3d.name: Onerion
description:f28c60204154f88557387b3d.text:
Prepare a powder of herbs and sleepless owl droppings for one drink, plus one additional drink per SL. Each must be consumed before the duration ends. The drinker’s next sleep contains one dream of your chosen kind, with details you specify or supplied by their subconscious. You can include a message, interpreted by the dreamer. Effects are psychological; a nightmare may cause a Fatigued Condition the following day.

Blood and Bramble p. 6: Hedgecraft spells require ingredients. A successful Lore (Herbalism) foraging roll provides 1 + SL ingredients; the printed purchase price is 5 brass pennies. Foraging and ingredient consumption are campaign references, not character-creation grants.

description:bbb6f76f63c472791b06d183.name: Stout Spirit
description:bbb6f76f63c472791b06d183.text:
Enchant up to 10 swigs of strong alcohol in a container. Each drinker automatically passes their first Fear Test during the duration. After this benefit, their effect ends and cannot benefit them again before the next dawn.

Blood and Bramble p. 6: Hedgecraft spells require ingredients. A successful Lore (Herbalism) foraging roll provides 1 + SL ingredients; the printed purchase price is 5 brass pennies. Foraging and ingredient consumption are campaign references, not character-creation grants.

description:489dd09d86cb7f966e9d8ba6.name: Trankraft
description:489dd09d86cb7f966e9d8ba6.text:
Enchant a bowl of hot broth for one person, who must immediately drink it all; some Hedgewise traditions also call for an appreciative burp. For the duration, the drinker ignores Fatigued Conditions from exertion or exposure, but not magic. Those Conditions return when the spell ends and remain until proper rest.

Blood and Bramble p. 6: Hedgecraft spells require ingredients. A successful Lore (Herbalism) foraging roll provides 1 + SL ingredients; the printed purchase price is 5 brass pennies. Foraging and ingredient consumption are campaign references, not character-creation grants.

description:64d6ae5919b78da7eec9e3c0.name: Woecharm
description:64d6ae5919b78da7eec9e3c0.text:
Infuse jewellery with ill will. Once willingly worn, it causes minor daily misfortunes and gives −10 to Gamble Tests, −10 to Tests resisting harmful magic, and +20 to Critical Wound severity rolls. Second Sight detects the curse only while an effect is occurring; Detect Artefact can identify it.

Blood and Bramble p. 6: Hedgecraft spells require ingredients. A successful Lore (Herbalism) foraging roll provides 1 + SL ingredients; the printed purchase price is 5 brass pennies. Foraging and ingredient consumption are campaign references, not character-creation grants.

description:0d48f736132728c26eb9824e.name: Godspakt
description:0d48f736132728c26eb9824e.text:
Choose a spirit and a task, then cast at a place resonant with that spirit. Success summons it to perform your request. Most demand payment, increasing with the task; the GM chooses the demand, which can involve material or unusual sacrifices.

Blood and Bramble p. 6: Hedgecraft spells require ingredients. A successful Lore (Herbalism) foraging roll provides 1 + SL ingredients; the printed purchase price is 5 brass pennies. Foraging and ingredient consumption are campaign references, not character-creation grants.

Source discrepancy: the quick-reference card on PDF p. 28 prints Range Touch and Target 1. The user selected the detailed p. 10 profile, Range You and Target You.

description:87ff8ed14039f74a89d173f5.name: Banishment of Böl
description:87ff8ed14039f74a89d173f5.text: Target a creature with Daemonic or Undead. If its Willpower is lower than yours, it turns its attention from you to whatever it would otherwise attack. Otherwise win an Opposed Cool Test for this effect. Its attention returns to you when the new target dies; you may cast again. Presenting a personal memento lets you direct it towards a particular suitable person instead.

description:f8200070f10c2d414f33c461.name: Bonesnapper
description:f8200070f10c2d414f33c461.text: Mark a stone from a ruined building or monument with your own blood. Throw it as a Rock or use it as an Improvised Weapon (Fourth Edition core p. 295). If it inflicts at least 1 Wound, the victim must pass Difficult (−1 SL) Endurance or suffer Broken Bone (Minor) at that location (Fourth Edition core p. 179), without a Critical Wound. The effect ends after causing one Broken Bone or when the duration expires.

description:5e15a64b42dc5c29372ed585.name: Congeal
description:5e15a64b42dc5c29372ed585.text: The target loses 1 + SL Bleeding Conditions. For each removed, you may give them one Fatigued Condition. If you impose any Fatigued Conditions, they must pass Challenging (+0 SL) Endurance or gain Unconscious. This spell cannot inflict Bleeding through the Lore of Witchcraft effect.

description:978b70171376eb5960db9336.name: Curse of the Treacherous Tongue
description:978b70171376eb5960db9336.text: Crush a dried deer or other ungulate tongue. Unless the target passes Hard (−2 SL) Cool, you choose the next sentence they speak. It uses their normal voice and delivery; you cannot force them to start speaking. After that sentence they regain control, know what they said without knowing why, and may contradict it. Listeners are not compelled to believe it.

description:86a07f6f3c86400d77de462d.name: Fatethief
description:86a07f6f3c86400d77de462d.text: The target Tests Hard (−2 SL) Endurance and loses 1 Fortune point either way. Failure also prevents gaining Fortune points for the duration.

description:aaef76b237f6fb10f5294bc8.name: Lodestone
description:aaef76b237f6fb10f5294bc8.text: Dip a lodestone or other magnetic material into the target’s blood, which must be no more than a day old. For the duration it points towards the blood’s owner while they live, without indicating distance. The spell targets the stone, so the owner’s Resistance (Magic) and similar protections do not apply.

description:b85848dd1f25846542d678a1.name: Mirrored Abyss
description:b85848dd1f25846542d678a1.text: Touch a reflective surface no larger than your Willpower Bonus in yards to make a portal into a dark, silent realm. Anyone entering is trapped and must pass Challenging (+0 SL) Endurance each day or disappear forever. Living prisoners may pass Challenging (+0 SL) Cool to appear in nearby reflective surfaces. A second casting can free them; other solutions may exist. Dispelling only closes an open portal and does not release prisoners.

description:7a01160a265cc9753d5fae48.name: Outcast’s Curse
description:7a01160a265cc9753d5fae48.text: Unless the target passes Challenging (+0 SL) Willpower, everyone meeting them feels suspicious and uneasy, and their Fellowship-based interaction Tests take −20 for the duration. Acquaintances can ignore the unease if they choose and have reason to suspect witchcraft. Second Sight and similar senses detect Dhar indistinguishable from a witch’s own residue.

description:8f2728ea59fb0ba28694af66.name: Pactbind
description:8f2728ea59fb0ba28694af66.text: Cut your hand with a ritually prepared Dhar-infused blade and state an agreement. Another living creature must willingly cut their hand with it and clasp yours, accepting the exact terms without amendment. Any commitments you state also bind you. Each subject must fulfil the literal agreement to the best of their ability; the GM interprets it. A subject receives one warning before a breach. Breaking it causes frailty until they make amends with the caster, or the other subject if the caster breached it: every Wound loss adds a Bleeding Condition, each Fatigued Condition becomes two, and Critical Wound severity rolls gain +40. Ordinary Dispel (Fourth Edition core p. 237) cannot remove it; effects specifically removing curses can. The caster immediately senses its removal.

description:cbacefacba453db379fe5271.name: Painjar
description:cbacefacba453db379fe5271.text: Use a dying creature’s preserved pain, such as its bottled last breath. A target failing Hard (−2 SL) Cool rolls a random hit location and Critical Wound. It suffers the result’s other penalties for the duration, including apparent lost limbs, Stunned or Prone, but no extra Wounds or Bleeding Conditions. The injury appears real only to the victim. All these effects end with the spell; the GM may impose a further Stunned Condition for trauma.

description:6b48bbaf8e1c7339754b32c8.name: Wayward Path
description:6b48bbaf8e1c7339754b32c8.text: Walk the entire chosen path while chewing herbs and offal. For the duration, anyone following that route becomes lost and returns to their starting point, whether following you or travelling independently. In settlements, only those taking your exact route are affected; crossing it does nothing. Those sensing the Winds recognise magic but remain lost until it is dispelled.

description:6b8afd221a9bc8f057203600.name: Nameless Summons
description:6b8afd221a9bc8f057203600.text:
Prepare a circle up to Willpower Bonus yards across and invite an entity without controlling its identity or conduct. After casting, Test Challenging (+0 SL) Cool and add its SL to 1d10 on the Nameless Summons table. The GM decides the entity, requests, demands and actions; it may demand payment or attack. It remains indefinitely while inside the circle. On leaving, it returns after up to its Willpower Bonus Rounds (minimum 1).

Nameless Summons table (p. 17), printed results: −5 or worse: a greater daemon’s forelimb drags you into its realm; Hostile; gift: your flesh, blood and soul. −4 to −0: a Lesser Daemon or powerful spirit (Cairn Wraith or Tomb Banshee); Hostile; immediate sacrifice of 1d10 living, sentient creatures. +0 to +4: a Lesser Daemon or powerful spirit; Neutral; sacrifice of one living, sentient creature. +5 to +9: a Lesser Daemon or powerful spirit; Favourable; promise of a future sacrifice or great service. +10 or better: a Greater Daemon interested in speaking rather than killing outright; Neutral if demands are met, Hostile otherwise; future great service and your essence at death. Printed ambiguity: −0 and +0 overlap. Both rows are preserved as reference text; the GM must resolve result 0. The creator does not roll summons or grant an entity.

description:1918d7892514fc336df14948.name: Arboreal
description:1918d7892514fc336df14948.text: In woodland, add Agility Bonus SL to the creature's Stealth and Climb Tests.

description:5a9e2798a72cb0aa0a181bb8.name: Class Trappings Table
description:5a9e2798a72cb0aa0a181bb8.text:
| Class | Trappings |
| --- | --- |
| Academics | Sling Bag containing Writing Kit and 1d10 sheets of Parchment |
| Burghers | Cloak, Hat, Sling Bag containing Lunch |
| Courtiers | Fine Clothing, Tweezers, Ear Pick, and a Comb |
| Peasants | Cloak, Sling Bag containing Rations (1 day) |
| Rangers | Cloak, Backpack containing Tinderbox, Blanket, Rations (1 day) |

description:023b55000b9b5db07c614e37.name: Starting Wealth
description:023b55000b9b5db07c614e37.text:
| Status Tier | Wealth |
| --- | --- |
| Brass | 20 brass pennies plus 2d10 per Standing Level |
| Silver | 10 silver shillings plus 1d10 per Standing Level |
| Gold | 2 gold crowns plus 1 per Standing Level |

Keep duplicate starting items as spares; they may be sold. Examples: Brass 3 gives 6d10+20 brass pennies; Silver 3 gives 3d10+10 silver shillings; Gold 3 gives 5 gold crowns. Spend or save this money; Chapter 11 gives items and coin values.

description:40b487d2ae7fa249a6733f18.name: Common Forms Of Skullduggery
description:40b487d2ae7fa249a6733f18.text:
| Action | Test |
| --- | --- |
| Pick a pocket | Sleight of Hand opposed by the target’s Perception. |
| Force open a door or window | Strength for speed; with suitable tools, Stealth (Urban) for silence. |
| Pick a lock | Pick Lock; lock quality sets Difficulty. Harder locks may require Extended Tests once per round or minute. |
| Connect with local criminals | Difficult (-1 SL) Gossip; Criminal grants Advantage. |
| Argue your innocence | Charm opposed by Cool, or opposed Lore (Law) in court. Disadvantage if caught in the act or incriminating evidence exists. |
| Cheat at cards | Sleight of Hand opposed by Perception; success grants Advantage to your next Gamble Test in that game. |
| Bribe a guard | Bribery identifies a willing recipient and Status-based price; Haggle may reduce it. |
| Learn a thing’s value | Evaluate for value; Difficult (-1 SL) Evaluate to identify a room’s most valuable object quickly. |

description:4729f49798e5976b75370470.name: Example Difficulties Of Common Underhanded Tasks
description:4729f49798e5976b75370470.text:
| Difficulty | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Very Easy (+6 SL) | Sleight of Hand: take bread from a helpless child. Charm: persuade an already furious mob to burn an object. Bribe: locate a corrupt dockside tax inspector in Übersreik. |
| Easy (+4 SL) | Stealth (Urban): disappear into a crowded night street. Lore (Law): establish that suspicion alone does not justify arrest. Intimidate: deter a common thief with superior arms. |
| Average (+2 SL) | Sleight of Hand: perform a familiar shell-game scam. Perception: notice an ogre on a nearby street. Gossip: identify a wealthy potential victim. |
| Challenging (+0 SL) | Gamble: win a few shillings from bored merchants. Charm: recruit thieves to teach you. Stealth (Rural): enter a noble’s manor unseen. |
| Difficult (-1 SL) | Evaluate: distinguish an authentic masterpiece among forgeries. Intimidate: demand protection money from a dwarf. Charm: persuade an angry mob to burn a person. |
| Hard (-2 SL) | Lore (Law): make a Witch Hunter honour a Wizard’s Licence. Gossip: circulate a false story about a famous knight’s wooden leg. Charm: sell a merchant a bridge fraudulently. |
| Very Hard (-3 SL) | Intimidate: drive a Shallyan away from her patient. Bribe: corrupt a Reiksguard Captain. Charm: persuade an angry mob to listen calmly. |

description:2cf69f5d911667995b52b90d.name: Lock Difficulty
description:2cf69f5d911667995b52b90d.text:
|  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- |

| Simple Latch | Average (+2 SL) | 2 |

| Dwarf-made Lock | Very Hard (–3 SL) | 8 |

description:172527c1006340d1dddff582.name: Selection of Traps
description:172527c1006340d1dddff582.text:
| Trap | Setting Difficulty | Setting Fumble | If Triggered |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Bucket of sewage balanced on door | Easy (+4 SL) Set Trap. | Setter gains Besmirched. | Target gains Besmirched. |
| Covered pit | Average (+2 SL) Set Trap; dig three hours per two yards of depth. | Setter falls the pit’s depth. | Target falls the pit’s depth. |
| Mantrap (page 310) | Easy (+4 SL) Set Trap; 5 minutes. | Setter takes 6 Arm Damage. | Target takes 1d10 + 5 to a Leg and 1 Entangled, Strength 55. |
| Pulling aside a branch triggers dropping rock | Challenging (+0 SL) Set Trap. | Setter takes 4 Damage at a random Location. | Target takes 1d10 + 5 Head Damage and 1 Stunned. |
| Loose floorboard triggers a swinging blade | Difficult (−1 SL) Set Trap; one hour and a bladed weapon. | Setter takes 5 Damage at a random Location. | Target and everyone within 2 yards take 1d10 + weapon Damage at random locations. |

description:35783b9e907ad92ea5b055ba.name: Trap Spot Difficulty
description:35783b9e907ad92ea5b055ba.text:
| Set Trap Result | Perception Test Difficulty |
| --- | --- |
| Astounding Success (+5 or more SL) | Very Hard (−3 SL) |
| Impressive Success (+3 to +4 SL) | Hard (−2 SL) |
| Success (+1 to +2 SL) | Difficult (−1 SL) |
| Marginal Success (+0 SL) | Challenging (+0 SL) |

Use Challenging (+0 SL) when Difficulty is unspecified or the setter is unknown or long gone. Obvious traps or those in barren, open areas with little concealment may require Average (+2 SL) Perception or easier.

description:85acf647a64ac61d4775d81b.name: Common Social Tests
description:85acf647a64ac61d4775d81b.text:
| Action | Test |
| --- | --- |
| Befriend a useful contact | Charm to build rapport or learn preferences; success may reveal information or grant Advantage to a later Test. |
| Make someone Fear you | Intimidate opposed by the target’s Cool. |
| Carouse with some soldiers | Perform, Play or Entertain for songs, music or stories; Consume Alcohol to join drinking. |
| Convince someone to do what you want | Charm opposed by Cool. Suitable Lore may replace Charm in intellectual debate. Intimidate can compel short-term compliance with later repercussions. |
| Talk your way in to a gathering | Charm opposed by Cool; appearance and the credibility of your explanation affect Difficulty. |
| Inspire a crowd | Charm opposed by the audience’s lowest Cool. Leadership works in military settings or where you hold authority. |
| Read the Room | Intuition to assess mood, leadership, followers and fears. |
| Lying | Cool, Charm or Entertain (Acting), opposed by the listener’s Intuition. |
| Spread a Nasty Rumour | Gossip; plausibility and supporting evidence determine Difficulty. |
| Negotiate a Discount | Haggle for a better price. |

description:f94133b186996d012652545e.name: Example Difficulties Of Common Social Actions
description:f94133b186996d012652545e.text:
| Difficulty | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Very Easy (+6 SL) | Charm: tempt a habitual gambler into one more double-or-nothing hand. Entertain (Singing): lead a tavern in a favourite bawdy song. Consume Alcohol: socialise with soldiers returning from patrol. |
| Easy (+4 SL) | Charm: befriend a hungry student over a meal you bought. Intimidate: deter a cowardly noble from a duel. Play (Lute): perform well enough for modest brass earnings. |
| Average (+2 SL) | Charm: avoid an underpaid guard’s search. Intuition: recognise a dubious business proposition as fraud. Leadership: organise disciplined troops to march. |
| Challenging (+0 SL) | Charm: spend a day begging for a few brass pennies. Intimidate: deter a petty thief. Gossip: circulate a merchant’s supposed bankruptcy. |
| Difficult (-1 SL) | Leadership: hold troops against cavalry. Charm: obtain a hearing from an enemy soldier before an attack. Consume Alcohol: keep pace with a dwarf. |
| Hard (-2 SL) | Perform (Juggling): entertain a ruthless noble under threat of a sword. Haggle: obtain a blacksmith’s discount before a siege. Intimidate: persuade an ogre of your toughness. |
| Very Hard (-3 SL) | Play (Bagpipe): impress Altdorf’s court memorably. Charm: stop a courtier disparaging you after you leave. Intuition: read a reserved dwarf longbeard. |

description:b8db508f119317e7059eb731.name: Social Test Difficulty Factors
description:b8db508f119317e7059eb731.text:
| Factor | Easier | Harder |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Relationship | Friend or ally | Rival or enemy |
| Request | Modest demand | Difficult or burdensome demand |
| Stakes | Little at stake | Reputation or livelihood threatened |
| Costs | Little cost | Substantial time or money |
| Risks | Few risks | Injury or death possible |

description:7f6334a07f3838caa4b17f03.name: Stinking Drunk
description:7f6334a07f3838caa4b17f03.text:
| 1d10 | Outcome |
| --- | --- |
| 1–2 | ‘Marienburger’s Courage!’: +2 SL to resist Fear. |
| 3–4 | ‘You’re My Besht Mate!’: Ignore existing Animosities (page 183). |
| 5–6 | ‘Why’s Everything Wobbling!’: Each Turn, either Move or take an Action (page 162). |
| 7–8 | ‘I’ll Take Yer All On!’: Gain Animosity (Everybody!) (page 183). |
| 9–10 | ‘How Did I Get Here?’: Wake the next day hungover with little memory; companions or investigation may reveal events. Fail Consume Alcohol and also gain Poisoned (page 186). |

description:3db3f932ac5666d3fe1a6c28.name: Common Means Of Investigation And Research
description:3db3f932ac5666d3fe1a6c28.text:
| Action | Test |
| --- | --- |
| Tell how an animal died | Average (+2 SL) Animal Care; Challenging (+0 SL) for subtle poison or illness. |
| Tell a lie, or spot one | Charm opposed by Intuition; an implausible lie can increase Difficulty. |
| Ask around about someone | Gossip reveals opinions, with better results finding more secret or relevant details. Bribery identifies willingness to accept a bribe and a possible price. |
| Wring a secret from someone | Charm or Intimidate opposed by Cool; sensitivity of the information sets Difficulty. |
| Search a room or a crime scene | Perception reveals hidden details, with better results adding information. Disturbance increases Difficulty. |
| Extract information from books | Research identifies relevant libraries or books, or finds pertinent facts within them. |
| Recall a useful fact | An Advance in the appropriate Lore supplies basic facts; only obscure or unusual information needs a Test. |
| Spot a forgery | Evaluate, with Difficulty based on craftsmanship. |
| Follow someone’s trail | Track, with Difficulty based on conditions and trail age; oppose the quarry’s Track only if they concealed the trail. |

description:7b1522d70d69e8f0d6a0cd00.name: Example Difficulties Of Common Investigative Tasks
description:7b1522d70d69e8f0d6a0cd00.text:
| Difficulty | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Very Easy (+6 SL) | Gossip: identify the town’s most disliked person. Track: follow a wounded fawn through woods. Charm: persuade a drunk friend you will repay tomorrow. |
| Easy (+4 SL) | Evaluate: identify a misspelt property deed as forged. Research: recall that baronial deeds sit in the graf’s vault. Intimidate: obtain an accomplice’s name from a cowardly thief. |
| Average (+2 SL) | Track: follow a bandit across soft ground. Lore (Magic): recall the eight Winds’ colours and properties. Lore (History): recall Sigmar’s general life story. |
| Challenging (+0 SL) | Bribery: judge whether a guard will free a thief for payment. Charm: convincingly claim a different Imperial origin. Track: follow a fresh field or woodland trail. |
| Difficult (-1 SL) | Evaluate: notice incorrect ink on an otherwise excellent forgery. Perception: see a blood speck on a passing servant. Intuition: separate truth from lies in a merchant’s pitch. |
| Hard (-2 SL) | Research: find a daemon’s true name in a deranged wizard’s grimoire. Lore (Law): recall a decisive precedent. Track: follow a day-old trail over bare rocky mountains. |
| Very Hard (-3 SL) | Research: uncover a dwarf grudge’s full basis. Perception: notice one missing book on a huge shelf. Lore (Reikland): name every cousin of Karl Franz. |

description:cb4c2d909ef0fa73a6236eb5.name: Common Lore Specialisations
description:cb4c2d909ef0fa73a6236eb5.text:
| Specialisation | Information Provided |
| --- | --- |
| Engineering | Simple machinery, artisan identification and complex machines’ operating principles. |
| Geology | Stone identification, promising well or mine sites, and flood or collapse risks in caves. |
| Heraldry | Noble and military insignia, including coat-of-arms symbolism. |
| History | Relevant historical facts. |
| Law | Legal rules, loopholes, arguments and weaknesses in arguments. |
| Magic | Winds and their effects, magical traditions’ equipment, and whether a grimoire holds real spells. |
| Metallurgy | Metal and alloy identification, forging methods and repairs. |
| Science | Natural phenomena and theories for unusual compounds, including black powder and soap. |
| Theology | Beliefs and practices of religions familiar to your culture, including Imperial or elven gods. |

description:0e514aad000fba81a3d3418a.name: Languages and language families
description:0e514aad000fba81a3d3418a.text:
| Language | Family | Spoken by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Albion | None | Albion’s inhabitants. |
| Battle Tongue | None | Old World warriors; commands and gestures. |
| Bretonnian | Haffennaff Reikspiel, Wastelander | Bretonnia’s inhabitants. |
| Classical | Estalian, Tilean | Human scholars; common in Imperial scholarship, grimoires and holy texts. |
| Elthárin | None | Elves of Athel Loren, Laurelorn and Ulthuan; tonal with many dialects and difficult for non-elves. |
| Estalian | Classical, Tilean | Estalia’s inhabitants. |
| Gospodarinyi | Górelsk, Ungol | Most Kislevites; also called Kislevarin or Kislevite. |
| Grumbarth | None | Ogres; occasionally mercenary commanders. |
| Guilder | None | Appropriate trade-guild members; specialised slang protects trade secrets. |
| Haffennaff | Bretonnian, Reikspiel, Wastelander | Mootland halflings; also called Mootish. |
| Khazalid | None | Dwarfs of Karaz Ankor and many members of Sigmar’s cult. |
| Magick | None | Spellcasters; tonal languages shape magic rather than communicate. |
| Norse | None | Norscans; also widespread in Nordland, Ostland, Wasteland and Kislev. |
| Pilgrim Sign | None | Silent pilgrims and holy people; a full sign language also learned by deaf people. |
| Reikspiel | Bretonnian, Haffennaff Wastelander | Imperial inhabitants; the usual game language. |
| Queekish | None | Skaven of the Under-empire. |
| Tilean | Classical, Estalian | Tileans, including traders and mercenaries visiting the Empire. |
| Thieves Tongue | None | Old World street communities; highly local variants. |
| Wastelander | Bretonnian, Haffennaff Reikspiel | Rural Wasteland inhabitants; Marienburg officially uses Reikspiel. |

description:4f5028ef928d8a13e81ca231.name: Example Navigation Difficulties
description:4f5028ef928d8a13e81ca231.text:
| Difficulty | Conditions |
| --- | --- |
| Very Easy (+6 SL) | Fair-weather evening walk on a well-used path. |
| Easy (+4 SL) | Brief hill hike or ride to a neighbouring town. |
| Average (+2 SL) | Day journey across open ground or a forest with a map or at least one Advance in relevant Lore (Local). |
| Challenging (+0 SL) | Two-day journey to a known but unvisited place, or a short trip on a busy Talabec stretch. |
| Difficult (-1 SL) | Hurried night ride on little-used roads, or searching the trackless Barren Hills for a rumoured chapel. |
| Hard (-2 SL) | Searching Mirror Moors for gnome settlements, or descending a river with rapids and submerged rocks. |
| Very Hard (-3 SL) | Ill-supplied journey through hot Lustrian jungle, or hours climbing out of a dark cavern without light. |

| --- | --- | --- | --- |

description:536fc77630f6d4e20491294a.name: Remedy Effectiveness
description:536fc77630f6d4e20491294a.text:
| SL | Result |
| --- | --- |
| +6 or more, or Critical | Alleviate the Symptom for TB days. |
| +1 to +5 | Alleviate the Symptom for 24 hours. |
| +0 | Alleviate the Symptom for 24 hours, with an embarrassing side effect such as hiccups or a green tongue. |
| −0 | No useful remedy; if the patient fails Average (+2 SL) Cool, placebo relief lets them ignore the Symptom for 2d10 hours. |
| −1 to −5 | No effect. |
| −6 or less, or Fumble | No relief; also Test for Galloping Trots. |

description:a4157d2b491870c7e46c261d.name: Selection Of Poisons
description:a4157d2b491870c7e46c261d.text:
| Name | Source | Resistance Test | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Adder root | Mashed roots of widespread plant (Herbs) | Challenging (+0 SL) Endurance Test if ingested | For -SL hours, become Stinking Drunk (page 145) and gain 1 Stunned per -SL. |
| Black lotus (leaves) | Dried leaves of plant native to the Southlands (must be purchased) | Difficult (-1 SL) Endurance Test upon inhalation | Gain 2 Stunned, plus 1 per -SL. |
| Black lotus (sap) | Sap of plant native to the Southlands (must be purchased) | Difficult (-1 SL) Endurance Test upon suffering at least 1 Wound from a sap-coated blade | Gain 2 Poisoned, plus 1 per -SL. |
| Daemon’s tand | Fungus common to wetlands in the Old World (Herbs) | Hard (-2 SL) Endurance Test if ingested | Failure causes Convulsions and Fever for 2d10 hours. |
| Dwarf bile | Fungus common to the Worlds Edge Mountains (Herbs) | Challenging (+0 SL) Endurance Test if ingested | Failure causes Malaise and Nausea for 2d10 hours. |
| Juck | Paste made from woodland plant harvested in spring (Herbs) | Average (+2 SL) Endurance Test if smeared onto skin | Pox lasts 40 minutes plus 10 minutes per -SL. |
| Rat poison | Heating ruby sulphur (Chemistry) | Difficult (-1 SL) Endurance Test if ingested | Gain Besmirched and 2 Poisoned. |
| Schlafenkraut | Infusion of dried leaves of wetland plant (Herbs) | Difficult (-1 SL) Endurance Test if ingested | Gain 1 Fatigued plus 1 per -SL; exceeding Toughness Bonus in Fatigued Conditions causes deep sleep. |
| Spider spittle | Concentrated giant spider venom (Chemistry) | Challenging (+0 SL) Endurance Test on taking 1 Wound from envenomed blade | Gain 1 Poisoned. |
| Weirdroot | Sliced bulbs of widespread plant (Herbs) | Very Easy (+6 SL) Endurance Test if ingested | For 2d10 hours: unless Fumbled, gain 1 Blinded and +2 SL to Psychology Tests; on a Fumble, become Stinking Drunk (page 145), with 2 Blinded and 2 Deafened. |

description:17fc8e5e56907d9010055ec4.name: Example Difficulties Of Common Movement Actions
description:17fc8e5e56907d9010055ec4.text:
| Difficulty | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Very Easy (+6 SL) | Ride (Horse): trot calmly across a meadow. Drive: negotiate a minor obstacle. Athletics: hurry across town before a shop sells out. |
| Easy (+4 SL) | Climb: use a maintained ladder. Swim: cross deep still water. Row: take a tender from a moored barge to dock. |
| Average (+2 SL) | Sail: set fore and mainsails in a light breeze. Climb: ascend a steep rope-assisted slope. Ride (Horse): reach a full gallop. |
| Challenging (+0 SL) | Ride (Demigryph): join a close parade formation. Athletics: enter a second-storey window via a brick wall. Drive: flee bandits at speed. |
| Difficult (-1 SL) | Climb: cross loose wet roof tiles. Sail: tack against strong wind. Swim: travel upstream in fast water. |
| Hard (-2 SL) | Ride (Demigryph): charge into spears. Drive: stop a damaged cart before a ditch. Row: escape a hungry stirpike. |
| Very Hard (-3 SL) | Ride (Horse): jump a broken bridge. Climb: ascend smooth mountain granite in rain. Swim: survive a waterfall descent unharmed. |

description:beef68f95c51827a87d07428.name: Obstacle Table
description:beef68f95c51827a87d07428.text:

| 1d10 | Result |

| 1–2 | Lose 1 Wound, ignoring Toughness Bonus and Armour Points. |

| 10 | Hit one random ally in range; the rolled units die gives hit SL. If impossible, gain Stunned after hitting yourself (page 186). |

description:a34a3dca8fe921155636d7a2.name: Melee Attack Modifiers
description:a34a3dca8fe921155636d7a2.text:

| Target is Surprised (+1 SL) | Attacker is in an enclosed space with a weapon of Average (-1 SL) or greater (-2 SL) reach. |

description:b60b9630bb474c19194dd53b.text:

| Target is Surprised (+1 SL) | Target is in cover or Prone (-1 SL) |
| You spent an Action last Turn aiming at the target (+1 SL) | Fog or poor lighting (-1 SL), rain and wind (-2 SL) or extreme weather or pitch blackness (-3 SL) |

description:f954a16c05719246e67322c2.name: Scatter
description:f954a16c05719246e67322c2.text:
After failed Ranged (Throwing), roll 1d10; T marks the target.

|  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 2 | 3 |

| 6 | 7 | 8 |

description:7216317fb67954cfe1890f47.name: Regional Events Table
description:7216317fb67954cfe1890f47.text:
The GM rolls one Regional Event for downtime, or substitutes an important local event, festival, misfortune or rumour relevant to a future adventure.

01–02: Grand Procession — The GM chooses the honoured Imperial god. Followers may make one Test with Advantage during the next adventure.

03–04: Unusual Mercenaries — Training or Unusual Learning with the visiting mercenaries reduces martial Skill or Talent training costs by 20%.

05–07: Auguries of the West Wind — Azyr Casting and Channelling gain +1 SL throughout the next adventure.

08–12: Teacher, Teacher! — The GM chooses an Advanced Skill; this downtime, Training can teach it without Consult an Expert to locate a tutor.

13–16: The Doktor is In — Improve Scarce and Rare Herbs and Draughts Availability one step this downtime (page 314). The visitor offers free amputations, extractions and haircuts.

17–21: Artisan Caravan — All Crafting Endeavour Tests gain +2 SL this downtime.

22–26: Flowing Profit — Riverfolk Income Endeavours earn 50% more this downtime.

27–30: Opportunity Saunters Through — Burgher and Peasant Income Endeavours earn 50% more this downtime.

31–35: Festivities — This downtime, Gossip has Advantage; Artists and Entertainers double Income Endeavour earnings.

36–39: Marvellous Miracle Cures — Improve Scarce and Rare Herbs and Draughts Availability one step when buying from the visitor this downtime (page 314). For each purchase the GM rolls d10: 1 or 2 replaces it with a GM-chosen Poison (page 313).

40–42: Levy — Warrior Income Endeavours earn 50% more and also count as Combat Training.

43–45: Travelling Players — Consult an Expert, Foment Dissent and The Latest News each cost one additional Endeavour this downtime.

46–52: Inclement Weather — During the next adventure, social Skill Tests suffer -1 SL and food costs 50% more.

53–55: Religious Mania — Pray Tests have Advantage this downtime.

56–59: Power Vacuum — Foment Dissent costs 1 Endeavour rather than 2 this downtime.

60–64: New Moon — Rogue Income Endeavours earn 50% more this downtime.

65–68: False Silver — Banking loses 20% of deposits; Income earnings also fall by 20%.

69–73: Tax Collector — Legal employment Income earnings fall by 50%; Rogues and other illegal workers earn twice normal Income.

74–81: Crime Crackdown — Rogue Income earns nothing. Rogues using Banking may choose only high-risk deposits.

82–88: Glorious Weather — During the next adventure, social Skill Tests suffer -1 SL; improve all non-Exotic goods’ Availability one step.

89–91: Local Crop Failure — Peasants cannot take Income; local food prices double for the next adventure.

92–94: Malicious Malady — Each Character passes Easy (+4 SL) Endurance or contracts Bloody Flux (page 180).

95–97: Riots — Courtiers cannot take Income. Foment Dissent Tests have Advantage.

98–00: Under Suspicion — Each Character loses one Endeavour hiding or proving innocence to the magistrate. Rogues cannot take Income until after their next adventure.

description:f5a1e51b6cb8914c26ef18ee.name: Character Events Table
description:f5a1e51b6cb8914c26ef18ee.text:
Each player rolls d100 for a downtime Character Event; effects may alter Endeavours or the next adventure.

01–04: Inspiration Strikes — Gain 50 XP.

05–09: Unexpected Esteem — Receive a reward appropriate to a previous good deed, available at the next adventure’s start. The GM determines the gift and may attach a complication.

10–14: Somebody Else’s Problem — Gain 1 additional Endeavour this downtime.

15–19: A Quiet Week — Ignore the first Fumble or Minor Miscast suffered during the next adventure.

20–24: A Good Day’s Work — For Income this downtime, increase Standing by 3 when determining earnings.

25–26: Is that an Original von Klapper? — Immediately sell one GM-chosen Trapping to a collector for twice its listed value, if desired.

27–29: Morr’s Embrace — Receive an inheritance before Endeavours: Brass, 20 brass pennies; Silver, 10 silver shillings; Gold, 2 gold crowns. Spend or bank it before the next adventure under Money to Burn.

30–34: Forewarned is Forearmed — Increase maximum Fortune by 1 for the next adventure.

35–41: What a Bargain! — Buy one Trapping at half its usual price.

42–47: Pedlar — Pay 6 d for ale to take Latest News without spending an Endeavour.

48–51: A Useful Connection — Take Commission or Research Lore without spending an Endeavour; associated Tests have Advantage.

52–56: Soothsayer — Pay 1 shilling to gain Doomed if absent, or replace an existing Dooming with a new page 118 roll. The fortune-teller cannot be found again for companions’ readings.

57–59: Arcane Auction — Buy a book for 2 GC. It may contain GM-determined secrets; you or a chosen literate Character may also take Research Lore without spending an Endeavour, with Advantage on required Tests.

60–67: Oi! You spilled my pint! — The GM chooses an offended faction; social Tests with its members have Disadvantage during the next adventure.

68–74: Onerous Obligations — Lose 1 Endeavour this downtime.

75–79: Impounded — Spend 1 Endeavour recovering a GM-chosen Trapping, or start the next adventure without it.

80–84: Ranald’s Wrath — Reduce maximum Fortune by 1 during the next adventure.

85–90: Scandalous Rumours — Fortune cannot be spent on social Tests during the next adventure.

91–92: Betrayed! — Agree a betrayer and motive with the GM. They or their agents may obstruct you at least once next adventure; the GM decides whether reconciliation is possible.

93–97: Accused Ally — The GM chooses an ally accused of a crime. A Law Guild Licence holder may spend 1 Endeavour and pass Average (+2 SL) Lore (Law) to defend them; otherwise the party spends 3 Endeavours to secure acquittal or an alibi. A freed ally owes a Major Favour (page 200). Otherwise the GM assigns punishment, potentially execution.

98–00: They’re a Witch! — Spend 1 Endeavour and pass Difficult (-1 SL) Charm to clear your name. Failure or inaction attracts a witch hunter, who may interrupt adventures until you are cleared. Killing them confirms suspicion and draws their allies.

description:abd817dcef347be51a2cca74.name: Advance Career
description:abd817dcef347be51a2cca74.text: After acquiring the required Trappings, Talents and Advances, spend this Endeavour and 100 XP to gain the next Career level. Fill 10 tracker boxes for level two, 12 additional boxes for level three and 14 additional boxes for level four.

description:749e2571edddab53f04a7a86.name: Common Endeavours
description:749e2571edddab53f04a7a86.text: These Endeavours are generally available between adventures. The GM may limit availability according to downtime location and circumstances.

description:692454ba8b65d3daa09c6030.name: Endeavours
description:692454ba8b65d3daa09c6030.text: While not adventuring, choose one Endeavour per week, with a maximum of three per downtime period.

description:d253969eddab3f2247013138.name: Banking
description:d253969eddab3f2247013138.text:
Unbanked money remaining after Between Adventures is lost before the next adventure. Choose a Banking option.

Invest with Banking House: Silver or Gold Status only. Choose or roll 1–10 as both percentage interest and risk. Withdrawing requires a further Banking Endeavour, immediately or after later adventures. Roll 1d100: at or below the chosen risk, lose the entire deposit; above it, recover principal plus accrued interest. For example, risk 6 yields 6% interest and fails on 6 or less; 10 GC earns 12 silver shillings.

Stash the Loot: Any Status may hide money or entrust it to someone. Withdraw before an adventure without an Endeavour; roll 1d100. On 10 or less, lose the entire stash; otherwise recover the principal. Successful withdrawals are available at the next adventure’s start alongside Income earnings.

description:cbf898e5cf82b28828e08601.name: Change Career
description:cbf898e5cf82b28828e08601.text: Agree the new Career’s introductions, costs, permits and feasibility with the GM; Species restrictions still apply. Spend this Endeavour and 100 XP to change within your Class, or 200 XP to enter another Class.

description:f8e5e7568231d0393201c3dd.name: Combat Training
description:f8e5e7568231d0393201c3dd.text: Gain one reroll for a Melee or Ranged Skill Test during the next adventure. This Endeavour can be taken repeatedly.

description:f5ef6aa8964c0f1a54e9ebf4.name: Commission
description:f5ef6aa8964c0f1a54e9ebf4.text: Commission one Exotic or bespoke Trapping per Endeavour. Find a capable craftsperson or supplier first, using Consult an Expert if necessary. Order and pay the listed cost; collect after the next adventure. Each additional item needs another Commission.

description:9f5c6de7ca0c4d080453a53d.name: Consult an Expert
description:9f5c6de7ca0c4d080453a53d.text:
Consult an expert to support another Endeavour or obtain knowledge. If none is known, make Challenging (+0 SL) Gossip: success finds a genuine specialist; failure finds a self-proclaimed authority whose advice the GM determines. The GM sets payment or Favours (page 200), callable in later adventures or repaid with future Endeavours. Advice depends on the expert’s field, experience, bias and your questions.

When seeking knowledge rather than supporting another Endeavour, also record an Expert Reroll: use it once on a directly related Test before the next adventure ends.

description:5e825182e30c6597851444a2.name: Crafting
description:5e825182e30c6597851444a2.text: With the appropriate Trade Skill, Trade Tools, raw materials and workshop, make a Consumer Guide Trapping or another GM-approved item. Materials normally cost one quarter of its list price. Make an Extended Trade Test; the GM sets Difficulty, usually guided by Availability.

description:f71e6a37bc65d7e8bfecf7bd.name: Foment Dissent
description:f71e6a37bc65d7e8bfecf7bd.text:
Spend two Endeavours to build unrest against a person, group or institution; Agitators also count this as Income. Pass Average (+2 SL) Gossip, then Charm with Difficulty based on the target’s popularity. A hated noble may be Easy (+4 SL); a respected Shallyan hospice may be Hard (-2 SL). Failure of either Test ends the attempt.

Success allows a Charm Test next adventure to assemble a hostile crowd, at GM-set Difficulty. Success produces harassment and threats; Impressive or Astounding Success may trigger rioting or attempted burning. Failure produces no action; a severe failure may warn the target or allies. After successful dissent, redirecting the crowd during that adventure requires Charm two Difficulty steps harder.

description:71d4796dd612db2c7613b1d4.name: Earned Income
description:71d4796dd612db2c7613b1d4.text:
| Status Tier | Income |
| --- | --- |
| Brass | 2d10 brass pennies per Standing Level |
| Silver | 1d10 silver shillings per Standing Level |
| Gold | 1 gold crown per Standing Level |

If the Earning Test fails, roll normal earnings then halve them, rounding down. Events may modify income. Receive it after disposing of the previous adventure’s unspent money under Money to Burn. Example: a Brass 3 Prowler rolls 6d10; a failed Average (+2 SL) Stealth (Urban) Test halves 34 to 17 brass pennies.

description:6fbf1e42fa1e5560299a62b9.name: Income
description:6fbf1e42fa1e5560299a62b9.text: Make an Average (+2 SL) Test with the Earning Skill shown in bold italics at Career level one. Success earns income for your current Career level’s Status, using Earned Income.

description:680590134a23c169eb6a4b3f.name: Research Lore
description:680590134a23c169eb6a4b3f.text: Requires a suitable library, archive, guild record, temple or other knowledge source. Make Average (+2 SL) Research. Success reveals one useful, interesting or hidden fact about the chosen subject, plus one relevant fact per SL. Impressive or Astounding Failure supplies convincing false information. The GM may roll secretly.

description:40758a32e87a7edf159e8034.name: The Latest News
description:40758a32e87a7edf159e8034.text: Make Challenging (+0 SL) Gossip for news from elsewhere. Success gives an interesting rumour; SL sets detail and accuracy, and the GM chooses its subject. Impressive Failure supplies convincing false information. The GM may roll secretly.

description:bd2b67560da56e0ed8527408.name: Study a Mark
description:bd2b67560da56e0ed8527408.text: Observe a chosen criminal target and make Challenging (+0 SL) Perception, adjusted for the mark’s accessibility. Success grants Advantage to one Test involving that mark next adventure; record it. The GM also supplies information or misinformation according to SL. This Endeavour may be taken repeatedly.

description:f4ae3297d3a3dcc39b4403be.name: Training
description:f4ae3297d3a3dcc39b4403be.text: Train a Skill or Characteristic outside your Career by paying normal XP plus a tutor fee. For Basic Skills and Characteristics, pay pennies equal to XP; Advanced Skills cost twice that fee (page 191). Specialists may require Consult an Expert to locate a tutor. Some Lores require appropriate institutions; forbidden subjects may require an adventure to find a willing teacher, usually at greater cost and often a Significant Favour (page 200).

description:92bb47434c1d5cb2aa705a21.name: Unusual Learning
description:92bb47434c1d5cb2aa705a21.text: Learn the first level of an out-of-Career Talent; this cannot increase an existing Talent. Locate a suitable tutor, using Consult an Expert for obscure Talents or remote locations if needed. Training costs 4d10 silver shillings.

description:7835d4a7627c906d60e65b8e.name: Wrath of the Gods Table
description:7835d4a7627c906d60e65b8e.text:
Roll on a Pray Fumble or when its units die is at or below current Sin Points; the GM may also roll or choose a result for insulting a god. Add +10 per Sin Point, apply the result, then reduce Sin by 1, minimum 0.

| d100 | Result |
| --- | --- |
| 01–05 | Holy Visions: Fail Average (+2 SL) Cool and gain one Stunned; the GM describes the visions. |
| 06–10 | Think Over Your Deeds: For one week, successful Pray is capped at +0 SL. |
| 11–15 | Heed My Lessons: Pray suffers -1 SL for 1d10 + Sin Points Rounds. |
| 16–20 | Prove Your Devotion: Gain Prone until successful Average (+2 SL) Pray. |
| 21–25 | You Try My Patience: No Pray Tests for 1d10 Rounds. |
| 26–30 | You Do Not Understand My Intent: All GM-chosen deity-associated Skills suffer -1 SL for 1d10 + Sin Points hours. |
| 31–35 | Your Lack of Faith is a Sorrow to Me: No Pray Tests for 1d10 + Sin points Rounds. |
| 36–40 | Share My Pain: Lose 1 + Sin Points Wounds ignoring Toughness Bonus and Armour Points; fail Average (+2 SL) Endurance and also gain one Stunned. |
| 41–45 | Your Cause Is Unworthy: Allied targets gain Prone. The deity’s Blessings and Miracles targeting them fail for 1d10 + Sin Points days. |
| 46–50 | Cease Your Prattling: No Pray Tests for 2d10 + Sin points Rounds. |
| 51–55 | Feel My Wrath: Lose 1d10 + Sin Points Wounds; fail Challenging (+0 SL) Endurance and also gain one Stunned. |
| 56–60 | I Shall Not Aid You: One GM-chosen deity-associated Skill suffers -1 SL for 1d10 + Sin Points days. |
| 61–65 | Divine Wounds: Gain 1 + Sin Points Bleeding. |
| 66–70 | Struck Blind: Gain Prone and 3 Blinded. Only successful Challenging (+0 SL) Pray removes these Blinded, at 1 + SL per success. |
| 71–75 | What Will You Sacrifice?: Lose 1d10 + Sin Points Wounds ignoring Toughness Bonus and Armour Points; fail Difficult (-1 SL) Endurance and also gain one Stunned. |
| 76–80 | You Have Sinned Against Me: Use each Action for Pray for 1d10 + Sin Points Rounds. |
| 81–87 | Purge the Flesh: Lose 2d10 + Sin Points Wounds ignoring Toughness Bonus and Armour Points. Fail Hard (-2 SL) Endurance and gain one Stunned plus one per -1 SL. |
| 88 | Daemonic Interference: A Lesser Daemon appears within 2d10 yards and attacks the nearest target. |
| 89–95 | Fear My Wrath: Gain 1 + Sin Points Broken. |
| 96–100 | Go On Penance: Undertake a Penance. |
| 101–105 | Castigation: Reduce Wounds to 0 if higher; gain Unconscious until at least 1 Wound is restored. |
| 106–110 | Do Not Use My Name in Vain: Lose Bless and Invoke for 1d10 + Sin Points days. |
| 111–115 | Rely Not upon Your Vanities: Lose all Trappings; each completed Penance returns one taken magical item, if any. |
| 116–120 | You Abuse My Mercy: Lose Bless and Invoke for 2d10 + Sin Points days. |
| 121–125 | Behold Your Wickedness: Next normal Fortune refresh restores only 1 point. |
| 126–130 | Thunderbolts and Lightning: Reduce Wounds to 0 if higher; gain Ablaze. |
| 131–135 | Suffer as I Suffer: Gain 1 + Sin Points Bleeding each morning until completing a Penance. |
| 136–140 | Excommunication: Lose Bless and Invoke. First Penance restores Bless; second restores Invoke. Fellow cultists know; interactions are Very Hard (-3 SL), with no positive Difficulty adjustment. |
| 141–145 | Prove Your Worth: A Divine Servant appears within 1d100 yards and acts according to the god’s nature, potentially attacking, intervening or rebuking. |
| 146–150 | I Cast You Out: Permanently lose Bless, Invoke and all Pray Advances. Fellow cultists know; interactions are Very Hard (-3 SL), with no positive Difficulty adjustment. |
| 151+ | Called to Account: Summoned before the god; return requires spending a Fate Point. Return occurs at the GM’s chosen time and also applies I Cast You Out. |

description:e572a0f2a32ac415db1a2240.name: Types Of Magic In The Old World
description:e572a0f2a32ac415db1a2240.text:
| Specialisation | Used By | Concentrated In |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Aqshy | Spellcasters who study the Lore of Fire | Heat, major fires and intense anger. |
| Azyr | Spellcasters who study the Lore of Heavens | Elevated sites, mountain summits and tower tops. |
| Chamon | Spellcasters who study the Lore of Metal | Ore-rich mines, meteor craters and powerful forges. |
| Dhar | Witches, necromancers, daemonologists, Chaos sorcerers, beastmen bray-shamans | Recent battlefields, ancient ruins and profaned ritual sites. |
| Ghur | Spellcasters who study the Lore of Beasts | Untamed regions and beasts’ lairs. |
| Ghyran | Spellcasters who study the Lore of Life | Wild regions, jungles and flowing water. |
| Hysh | Spellcasters who study the Lore of Light | Sunlit windy plains and mountain peaks. |
| Magick | Hedge witches, witches | Spread throughout the world without concentrations. |
| Qhaysh | High elf mages, Slann mage-priests | Sites where all eight Winds unite. |
| Shyish | Spellcasters who study the Lore of Death | Battlefields, burial grounds, cairns and barrows. |
| Skaven | Skaven and harbingers of mutation | Warpstone and places it has corrupted. |
| Ulgu | Spellcasters who study the Lore of Shadows | Misty moors, shaded forests and caves. |
| Waaagh! | Orc and goblin shamans | Large orc and goblin gatherings. |

Channelling the specific power concentrated in an area grants Advantage to that Test.

description:036cf512d12871a2a0960ea4.name: Minor Miscast Table
description:036cf512d12871a2a0960ea4.text:
| d100 | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| 05 or less | Cloyed Tongue: All Language, including Casting, suffers –1 SL for 1d10 Rounds. |
| 06–10 | Witchsign: Mutate the next living creature born within 1 mile. |
| 11–15 | Driven to Distraction: In combat gain Surprised; otherwise lose concentration briefly through sudden alarm. |
| 16–20 | Intestinal Rebellion: Gain Besmirched. |
| 21–25 | Unfasten: All your buckles and laces open; belts, bags, pouches and armour may slip or fall. |
| 26–30 | Wayward Garb: Gain 1 Entangled, resisted against Strength 1d10 × 5. |
| 31–35 | Unholy Visions: Gain 1 Blinded; fail Challenging (+0 SL) Cool and gain another. |
| 36–40 | Soured Milk: All milk within 1d100 yards immediately spoils. |
| 41–45 | Freezing Breath: For 1 minute, those within Willpower Bonus yards pass Challenging (+0 SL) Endurance or suffer -1 SL to Ballistic Skill, Agility and Dexterity-based Tests until leaving. |
| 46–50 | Rupture: Gain 1 Bleeding. |
| 51–55 | Curse of Temperance: All alcohol within 1d100 yards spoils. |
| 56–60 | The Horror!: Fail Hard (-2 SL) Psychology and gain 1 Broken. |
| 61–65 | Darkling Sight: Lose Second Sight and suffer -2 SL Channelling for 1d10 hours. |
| 66–70 | Ululating Scream: Gain 1 Deafened lasting 1d10 Rounds. |
| 71–75 | Regurgitation: Gain Besmirched and 1 Stunned, with Stunned lasting 1d10 Rounds. |
| 76–80 | Fell Whispers: Fail Average (+2 SL) Cool and gain 1 Corruption Point. |
| 81–85 | Curse of Corruption: Gain 1 Corruption Point. |
| 86–90 | Marked by Magic: Gain a permanent physical mark associated with your Wind, commonly altered eyes. |
| 91–95 | Multiplying Misfortune: Roll twice more without modifiers, rerolling 91–00. |
| 96–00 | Cascading Chaos: Roll Major Miscast; positive modifier overflow beyond 00 carries to that roll. |

description:e061e1eadad3afcae589b2cf.name: Major Miscast Table
description:e061e1eadad3afcae589b2cf.text:
| d100 | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| 05 or less | Jibbering: For 1d10 Rounds, verbal communication and Language are unavailable; otherwise act normally. |
| 06–10 | Hellish Stench: Gain foul smell and Distracting (page 358) for 1d10 hours. |
| 11–15 | Ragdoll: Fly 1d10 yards in a random direction; land for 1d10 Damage ignoring Armour Points and gain Prone. |
| 16–20 | Power Drain: Cannot use the spell’s casting Talent, usually Arcane Magic, for 1d10 minutes. |
| 21–25 | Levitation: Hover 1d10 yards up for 1d10 minutes. Forced movement, spells or wings can move you, but otherwise you return to that position. Apply Falling when it ends (page 169). |
| 26–30 | Aethyric Shock: Lose 1d10 Wounds ignoring Toughness Bonus and Armour Points; fail Average (+2 SL) Endurance and also gain Stunned. |
| 31–35 | Chaos Quake: All within 1d100 yards pass Average (+2 SL) Athletics or gain Prone. |
| 36–40 | Hexeyes: Eyes take a Lore-associated colour for 1d10 hours. During this time, gain 1 irremovable Blinded and lose Magical Sense and Second Sight. |
| 41–45 | Limb Frozen: A random limb is unusable as if amputated (page 177) for 1d10 hours. |
| 46–50 | Death Walker: Plants you tread on die for 1d10 hours. |
| 51–55 | Aethyric Repulsion: Casting and Channelling suffer -3 SL for 2d10 hours. |
| 56–60 | Magefire: Gain Ablaze in Lore-coloured flames. |
| 61–65 | Swarmed: Engage a GM-chosen aethyric swarm, using the creature’s normal profile plus Swarm. Survivors retreat after 1d10 Rounds. |
| 66–70 | Chaotic Foresight: Gain 1 Fortune Point for the rest of the session; every Fortune Point spent causes 1 Corruption Point. |
| 71–75 | Blight: Willpower Bonus fields within Willpower Bonus miles lose crops overnight. |
| 76–80 | Foul Enfeeblement: Gain 1 Corruption Point, Fatigued and Prone. |
| 81–85 | Traitor’s Heart: Cannot regain Fortune until next downtime or until attacking or otherwise betraying another Character. |
| 86–90 | Ghostly Voices: You and all within Willpower Bonus yards pass Average (+2 SL) Cool or gain 1 Corruption Point. |
| 91–95 | Slipped from Memory: If memorised, lose the attempted spell and learn it again. |
| 96+ | Aethyric Feedback: Everyone within Willpower Bonus yards loses 1d10 Wounds ignoring Toughness Bonus and Armour Points, and gains Prone. With no targets in range, your head explodes and you die instantly. |

description:57d4e873e277ce2a5843a8ab.name: Travelling By Road
description:57d4e873e277ce2a5843a8ab.text:
| d10 | Encounter |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | Roadside Shrine: A shrine to Rhya, Taal or another god bears recent offerings. |
| 2 | Toll Gate: Two wardens collect tolls; one sleeps as the other argues over a farmer’s pigs. |
| 3 | Funeral Procession: A Morr priest leads mourners behind a shrouded corpse on a cart with a caged raven. |
| 4 | Gibbet: An old skeleton hangs beside a fresh warning against a crime. |
| 5 | Fellow Travellers: Roll Fellow Travellers for other road users. |
| 6 | Roadside Inn: A small coaching inn offers food and drink. |
| 7 | Beastman Totem: Bones, antlers and hides surround a marked tree with fresh blood beneath. |
| 8 | Marching Troops: Reikland pikemen pass; their officer orders you aside. |
| 9 | Corpse: An arrow-struck body lies ignored in the road. |
| 0 | Pyre: A body was burned at a roadside stake, then its forehead marked with a hammer or comet. |

description:9be7a3bd29ab5a736f8eb094.name: Travelling By River
description:9be7a3bd29ab5a736f8eb094.text:
| d10 | Encounter |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | Drowned Tree: A dead river tree bears offerings and Manann’s trident. |
| 2 | Ferry Crossing: People, livestock and priests crowd a ferry despite the ferryman’s assurances. |
| 3 | Dead Man’s Boat: An empty bloodstained rowboat drifts with a trailing rope. |
| 4 | Fisherman’s Catch: A fisherman cuts an alarming catch loose. |
| 5 | Fellow Travellers: Roll Fellow Travellers for other river users. |
| 6 | Plague Barge: A shuttered deserted boat sits at anchor behind white rope near a tended Shallyan shrine. |
| 7 | Waterborne Revels: A drunken barge crew cheers a barrel falling overboard; its unattended helm still clears a bend. |
| 8 | Abandoned Camp: Two overturned boats lie beside slashed tents and scattered belongings; nobody alive is visible. |
| 9 | Warning Shot: An arrow from wooded banks hits the boat; possible goblins or a wood elf warning against landing. |
| 0 | Riverbank Gallows: Three fresh corpses hang beneath a death warning for piracy and smuggling. |

description:2daefbe5c577944dee884ecb.name: Quick Armour

Apothecary books usually include Digestive Tonic, Healing Draught and Vitality Draught formulas; advanced volumes may cover rarer draughts.

Law books cover regional legislation; travelling legal collections may combine several areas.

Magic books may be locked or magically warded. Possession of a spell grimoire without a College licence is punishable as heresy.

Guild Licences are granted under guild rules rather than bought. Legal Documents include wills, IOUs and statements of intent.

Tools and workshop contents suit the trade. Apothecaries use ingredient-processing and measuring tools; carpenters use woodworking tools; engravers use cutting, marking and pressing equipment; smiths use metalworking tools and a forge. Artists use their medium’s tools and materials. Engineers use timing, measuring and drafting tools; herbalists use harvesting and preparation tools; navigators use astronomical, charting, timing and sounding instruments. Physicians use surgical tools, dressings and treatment facilities.
